===== aida findings promote
Promote a finding — sets status Approved and adds it to a work queue

Usage: aida findings promote [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>
          The finding's ID (UUID or SPEC-ID)

Options:
      --for <ROLE>
          Route the promoted finding to this role's work queue. Defaults to `implementer` — a
          promoted finding is implementation work

      --reason <TEXT>
          Rationale for the promotion ("more important than its priority suggests", "blocks another
          open PR", etc.). When provided, the rationale is appended as an audit comment so the *why*
          survives alongside the queue note

      --auto-complete
          When the finding's origin-ID fix has already merged to the default branch, bump the
          promoted spec straight to Completed instead of queueing it as fresh work. Without this
          flag, an already-merged origin-ID only prints a warning and the finding still queues

      --force
          Promote (and queue) even when the origin-ID fix already merged — for reopening or
          extending the finding. Suppresses the already-merged warning / auto-complete entirely

      --to <DEST>
          Destination: `work` (the default — fix this instance) or `gate` (gate the whole class).
          The gate destination is offered once the finding's recurrence count reaches the promote
          threshold
          
          [default: work]

      --detectable <ANSWER>
          Gate screening answer, required with `--to gate`: `mechanical` (a violation is
          recognisable without judgement), `agent` (only an agent could recognise it; its verdict is
          advisory), or `none` (stays prose — recorded so the question is not re-opened)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida findings calibration
Calibration review surface — list cold-boot vs fork-from-live advisor verdicts side-by-side. Default
view shows disagreements (the rows that name a substrate gap); `--all` widens to agreements too, and
`--stats` swaps the table for the rolling metric. Annotate one row with the `annotate` sub-action

Usage: aida findings calibration [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  annotate  Annotate a calibration record. The note is a one-line triage hint; the prefix categories
            `gap → wrote memory <name>`, `inherently in-flight, accept`, and `cold-boot was actually
            correct` feed the `--stats` histogram, but any text is accepted
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --since <WINDOW>
          Restrict to records since this point: a relative window (`7d`, `12h`, `2w`, `30m`, or `24
          hours ago`), an ISO date (`2026-05-01`, local midnight), a zone-less ISO datetime (local
          time), or RFC3339

      --agreement
          Show only records where the two advisors agreed

      --disagreement
          Show only records where the two advisors disagreed. The default (no flag) is equivalent —
          disagreements are the triage signal

      --all
          Show every record (agreements + disagreements + no-fork rows)

      --stats
          Print the rolling-metric summary (agreement rate over the last N records, 4-week trend,
          annotation-category histogram) instead of the per-record table

      --last <N>
          Number of records the `--stats` agreement rate considers. Default 50
          
          [default: 50]

===== aida questions
The async decision inbox — structured questions the advisor distilled from forks it couldn't
resolve, which you answer OUTSIDE any agent (plain CLI, no LLM session). Bare `aida questions` lists
the inbox and, at a TTY with pending items, offers to enter the answer loop; `aida questions list`
is the pure read; `aida questions answer` records answers. The recorded answer is a pure data op —
slice 1 records it, a later loop pass applies the chosen resolution

Usage: aida questions [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list     Run by: anyone, when: you want to see what's pending (read-only)
  sweep    Run by: advisor / automation, when: detecting which specs need a human decision before
           they're pickable (the detection pass)
  ask      Run by: the advisor, when: it hits a fork it can't resolve and needs to pose the question
           to the human (not a human-run command)
  clarify  Run by: human + agent together (interactive), when: an under-specified spec needs
           acceptance criteria authored before it's pickable
  remedy   Run by: TUI / advisor automation, when: a drive hold is only missing acceptance criteria
           and should be remedied without a manual clarify hop
  answer   Run by: the human, when: draining pending decisions (no LLM session — a plain operator
           data op)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

===== aida questions ask
Run by: the advisor, when: it hits a fork it can't resolve and needs to pose the question to the
human (not a human-run command).

Pose a structured DecisionRequest on a spec. The advisor distills a fork into a self-contained
question + enumerated choices, each mapping to a deterministic resolution token. Refuses if the spec
already has a pending request unless --force. Requires at least two choices.

Usage: aida questions ask [OPTIONS] --question <TEXT> <SPEC>

Arguments:
  <SPEC>
          The spec (UUID or SPEC-ID) the question is about

Options:
  -q, --question <TEXT>
          The self-contained question (no spec re-read needed to answer)

  -c, --choice <LABEL|CONSEQUENCE|RESOLUTION>
          A choice, as `label|consequence|resolution`. Repeatable; supply at least two. `resolution`
          is a deterministic action token (e.g. `status:rejected`, `tag:+deferred:post-stability`,
          `noop`) — never free-form prose

      --recommend <N>
          1-based index of the recommended default choice (stored 0-based)

      --rationale <TEXT>
          Why the recommended default is recommended

      --force
          Overwrite an existing pending DecisionRequest on this spec

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida questions answer
Run by: the human, when: draining pending decisions (no LLM session — a plain operator data op).

Answer pending decisions — the HUMAN-decision drain, the symmetric complement of `aida burndown run`
(which drains the decision-FREE ready set with autonomous agents). Answering APPLIES the chosen
resolution: it binds a design decision into the spec's `## Acceptance`, clears a disposition gate,
or rejects — then auto-queues the now decision-free spec onto the burndown ready set (advisor-gated;
honest about any remaining blocker). No agent, no LLM session — a pure operator data op.

`answer <spec> <choice>` records one answer non-interactively (choice is a 1-based number, or the
word `default`/`recommended`). `answer` with no args enters the interactive loop over all pending
(TTY) — the human-decision drain. `answer --all-defaults` confirms every recommended default at
once.

Usage: aida questions answer [OPTIONS] [SPEC] [CHOICE]

Arguments:
  [SPEC]
          The spec (UUID or SPEC-ID) to answer. Omit for the interactive loop

  [CHOICE]
          The chosen option: a 1-based number, or `default`/`recommended`

Options:
      --all-defaults
          Confirm the recommended default for every pending request that has one, in a single batch

      --note <TEXT>
          Attach a free-text counter-proposal recorded ALONGSIDE the chosen option (e.g. "name it
          list-claude-sessions"). A pure data op — no LLM at answer-time; the implementer reads
          choice + note later. The non-interactive form of the interactive prompt's "type something"
          escape; pair with <spec> <choice>

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida advisor
The advisor seat. Bare `aida advisor` prints the advisor's actionable worklist — the mirror of bare
`aida human`, but grouped by ADVISOR action (groom drafts, distill decisions, triage findings, bless
the queue, close delivered epics). Subcommands manage the live-advisor registration the
`--no-human=both` orchestrator reads, the dashboard, and scheduling

Usage: aida advisor [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  register    Record the current Claude session as the live advisor — writes `~/.aida/advisor.toml`.
              With no `--uuid`, reads `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` from the environment (Claude Code
              sets it on every session). Pass `--uuid <id>` to register a specific session id
  unregister  Clear the registration. Idempotent — succeeds even when nothing is registered
  watch       Presence-gated fork-from-live watch loop: while `away`, fork the live advisor only
              when `aida awaiting` is non-empty and run a garden + mailbox-triage + escalate pass
              headless. Opt-in by invocation; exits on `aida home` (or away-TTL). The forked advisor
              only does safe/bounded work and escalates the rest
  status      The advisor's read-only situational dashboard — one screen of counts, each row
              pointing at the canonical command to act on it: live-advisor readiness, intake drafts,
              pending decisions, findings, backlog, burndown readiness, queue depth, and live
              sessions. Pure aggregation of existing surfaces; writes nothing
  schedule    Recurring maintenance/research tasks that land in the queue on a cadence. No daemon:
              due schedules are evaluated and fired on every `aida pull`. Manage them with the
              subcommands below
  handoff     Generate a checked-in advisor handoff brief for a sibling project. Writes a dated,
              structured Markdown brief at `<to>/docs/<date>-advisor-handoff.md` with five sections
              — parent identity (auto), vision, decided things, substrate slice (scoped by
              `--focus`), and latitude. The brief is a template: parent identity and the focus topic
              are filled in automatically; the strategic sections are placeholders the operator
              authors before committing it to the child project
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --short
          Bare spec-ids from the worklist, one per line — usable in `$(...)` / xargs (mirrors `aida
          human --short`). Ignored when a subcommand is given

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when

      --once
          Run a single tick and exit (cron-friendly)

      --triage-only
          Conservative mode: the forked advisor still gardens but only surfaces/escalates mailbox
          items (never acts on a request)

      --poll-interval <POLL_INTERVAL>
          Seconds between presence re-checks (default 60)
          
          [default: 60]

      --fork-interval <FORK_INTERVAL>
          Deprecated compatibility flag. Forks are driven by `aida awaiting`, not elapsed time
          
          [default: 1200]

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida advisor status
The advisor's read-only situational dashboard — one screen of counts, each row pointing at the
canonical command to act on it: live-advisor readiness, intake drafts, pending decisions, findings,
backlog, burndown readiness, queue depth, and live sessions. Pure aggregation of existing surfaces;
writes nothing

Usage: aida advisor status [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json
          Emit the dashboard as JSON instead of the human summary

      --registration
          Show only the narrow live-advisor registration block (the pre-dashboard output) —

===== aida advisor schedule
Recurring maintenance/research tasks that land in the queue on a cadence. No daemon: due schedules
are evaluated and fired on every `aida pull`. Manage them with the subcommands below

Usage: aida advisor schedule [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  add      Register a recurring task. The schedule fires immediately on the next `aida pull`
           (never-fired schedules are due now), then on every cadence boundary thereafter
  list     List registered schedules with cadence, last-fired, next-due, status
  enable   Enable a disabled schedule so it resumes firing on cadence
  disable  Disable a schedule. It's preserved but never fired until re-enabled
  remove   Remove a schedule entirely
  run      Manually fire due schedules now (the same logic `aida pull` runs). With a name,
           force-fire that one schedule regardless of cadence
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida advisor schedule add
Register a recurring task. The schedule fires immediately on the next `aida pull` (never-fired
schedules are due now), then on every cadence boundary thereafter

Usage: aida advisor schedule add [OPTIONS] --every <EVERY> --template <TEMPLATE> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>
          Unique short name (the registration key). Becomes the `scheduled:<name>` tag on every
          filed TASK

Options:
      --every <EVERY>
          Cadence: a Go-duration-like token (`90d`, `14d`, `30d`, `12h`, `1w`). Units: m=minutes,
          h=hours, d=days, w=weeks

      --template <TEMPLATE>
          TASK title filed when the schedule fires

      --description <DESCRIPTION>
          TASK description (optional)

      --tags <TAGS>
          Extra comma-separated tags applied to the filed TASK (in addition to `scheduled:<name>`
          and `batch:scheduled`)

      --for <FOR_ROLE>
          Role the filed TASK is routed to. Defaults to `advisor`
          
          [default: advisor]

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida advisor handoff
Generate a checked-in advisor handoff brief for a sibling project. Writes a dated, structured
Markdown brief at `<to>/docs/<date>-advisor-handoff.md` with five sections — parent identity (auto),
vision, decided things, substrate slice (scoped by `--focus`), and latitude. The brief is a
template: parent identity and the focus topic are filled in automatically; the strategic sections
are placeholders the operator authors before committing it to the child project

Usage: aida advisor handoff [OPTIONS] --to <PROJECT> --focus <TOPIC>

Options:
      --to <PROJECT>
          Path to the sibling/child project the brief is for. The brief is written under
          `<to>/docs/`; the directory is created if absent

      --focus <TOPIC>
          The focus topic for this handoff — names the slice of advisor context the child project
          inherits (e.g. "git-canonical store", "orchestrator drain"). Used in the brief title and
          the substrate section heading

      --force
          Overwrite an existing brief for the same date instead of refusing. By default a same-day
          brief is preserved

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida punt
Punt a spec to Needs Attention — pause it with a structured reason instead of guessing past a
design-fork. The safety net an autonomous drain reaches for when it hits a decision it cannot safely
make

Usage: aida punt [OPTIONS] --category <CATEGORY> --reason <REASON> <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>
          The spec (UUID or SPEC-ID) to punt. Must currently be In Progress

Options:
  -c, --category <CATEGORY>
          The kind of obstacle. One of: design-fork, ambiguous-spec, missing-context,
          blocked-dependency, other

  -r, --reason <REASON>
          Human-readable description of the fork / obstacle that stopped you

  -l, --lean <LEAN>
          Optional best-guess answer if forced to choose — recorded distinctly from the reason so
          triage can see the agent's lean

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

===== aida punts
Browse and analyze the local design-fork punt ledger

Usage: aida punts [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list      Browse recent punt records from the ledger
  analyze   Print rolling metrics and stats for recent punts
  resolve   Resolve an open punt with a decision — writes the orchestrator resume response AND
            closes the ledger record
  dismiss   Dismiss an open punt as not needing a decision — closes the ledger record without
            resuming an implementer
  escalate  Escalate an open punt to a human — writes the orchestrator park response AND closes the
            ledger record as escalated-to-human
  read      Print the full ledger record for a spec
  promote   Extract a pattern from a punt into a new memory pack entry
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:

===== aida archive
Mark one or more requirements as archived (hidden from default views but preserved in graph
traversals and the audit trail).

Archive is a view-level flag distinct from status — a freshly Completed spec stays visible until
archived. Use `--older-than` for bulk sweeps over closed work; the default csv targets completed and
rejected statuses.

Usage: aida archive [OPTIONS] [ID]

Arguments:
  [ID]
          SPEC-ID to archive (mutually exclusive with --older-than)

Options:
      --older-than <DURATION>
          Bulk-archive every spec last touched before this point: a relative duration (`30d`, `12h`,
          `2w`, or `24 hours ago`), an ISO date (`2026-05-01`, local midnight), a zone-less ISO
          datetime (`2026-05-01T10:00`, local time), or RFC3339. Pairs with `--status`

      --status <CSV>
          Restrict the --older-than sweep to specs with one of these statuses (comma-separated).
          Default: completed,rejected

      --dry-run
          Print the sweep plan without writing — pairs with --older-than

      --force
          Skip the confirmation guard when archiving a non-terminal
          (Draft/Approved/Planned/InProgress) or queued spec, and allow the --older-than sweep to
          include non-terminal statuses. Archive is for the closed long-tail; this opts past that
          safety rail

      --verbose
          List each archived id during an --older-than sweep (instead of just the throttled progress
          tick + completion line)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida defer
Defer a spec — park it as primed/conditional work, hidden from the default open-work view but not
filed away the way archive is.

Defer is a view-level flag distinct from status (it does not touch the lifecycle state machine). Use
`--reason` to record why this is an operator hold and `--until` to record the revisit trigger — the
free-text condition that brings the spec back (e.g. `--until "when a slice verb ships"`). That
trigger is the one thing distinguishing deferred (prospective, primed) from archived (retrospective,
filed). Deferred rows are hidden from `aida list`, `aida search`, and `aida history` by default;
surface them with `--deferred` (only) or `--all` (union).

Usage: aida defer [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>
          SPEC-ID or UUID to defer

Options:
      --until <CONDITION>
          The revisit trigger — the condition that brings this spec back (free text). Stored
          alongside the spec and shown in the deferred view so you can scan what is primed and what
          returns each item

      --reason <REASON>
          Why the work is being held. Required for a durable operator hold; legacy deferrals may
          omit it

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida claim
Record a spec-scoped CLAIM so advisor-fanned work is visible to the duplicate-dispatch gates.

AIDA-launched work (`aida queue work`, `aida agent new --spec`) writes a spec-scoped session lease,
so a second pickup of the same spec is refused. But when an advisor fans an implementer via the
Claude Agent tool (a worktree-isolated subagent), that work takes only a generic `harness-worktree`
lease — NOT spec-scoped — so the gate can't see it. `aida claim <spec>` closes that gap: it writes a
lightweight advisory lease whose scope IS the spec id, keyed to the calling session's pid, so the
same gate now refuses a duplicate `aida queue work <spec>` and warns on `aida edit <spec>`.

Liveness-aware: the claim only holds while the claiming process is alive; a dead claimer's claim is
ignored (no crash-deadlock). Idempotent — re-claiming your own spec is a no-op refresh. Clear it
with `aida unclaim <spec>`. Surfaces in `aida status <spec>` and `aida ps`.

Usage: aida claim [OPTIONS] <SPEC>

Arguments:
  <SPEC>
          SPEC-ID, agreed-id, or UUID to claim

Options:
      --worktree <PATH>
          Optional worktree path to record on the claim (where the fanned implementer is working).
          Informational; the claim's liveness is the claiming process, not this path

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida unclaim
Inverse of `aida claim` — removes the caller's spec-scoped claim so a fresh `aida queue work <spec>`
/ `aida edit <spec>` no longer sees it

Usage: aida unclaim [OPTIONS] <SPEC>

Arguments:
  <SPEC>
          SPEC-ID, agreed-id, or UUID to unclaim

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when

===== aida db
Database management commands

Usage: aida db [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  path                   Print the path to the active store (the orphan-branch worktree, in
                         distributed mode). The legacy `--name` registry lookup was dropped in Phase
                         1 of the kernel/module audit
  info                   Show database statistics and info
  sync                   Sync git-backed store with remote (push/pull)
  merge-gate             Assign agreed IDs (short IDs) to all objects that don't have one. Run this
                         at merge-to-trunk to collapse a node-aware distributed id (e.g. `FR-N-NNN`)
                         down to its short form (`FR-NNN`)
  retire-legacy-ids      Collapse legacy origin spec_ids onto their agreed_ids. For each requirement
                         where spec_id ≠ agreed_id (typically a legacy zero-padded origin id with a
                         later-assigned short agreed id), set spec_id := agreed_id and clear
                         agreed_id. The on-disk YAML moves to the new sharded path; relationships
                         are unaffected (they use UUIDs). Run with --dry-run first to preview
  workspace-init         Initialize a multi-repo workspace (multiple code repos sharing one store)
  status                 Show status of the git-backed store (changes, sync state, conflicts)
  block                  Manage pre-allocated agreed ID blocks for offline-safe trace comments
  reconcile-status       Replay the Done → Completed auto-bump scan over a wider commit range than
                         `aida pull` saw, recovering specs that got stranded at Done. The pull-time
                         auto-bump only scans commits the current pull brings in; if a spec's YAML
                         was unreadable at pull time, or the user pulled before flipping the spec to
                         Done, the bump silently misses and the spec is stuck without manual
                         intervention
  check                  Audit the store for consistency problems. Currently supports `--collisions`
                         (two requirements claiming the same short id, which the gate-time check
                         prevents going forward but doesn't retroactively detect)
  migrate-related-edges  Repair custom edges that graph traversals do not follow
  help                   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

collapse a node-aware distributed id (e.g. `FR-N-NNN`) down to its short form (`FR-NNN`)

Usage: aida db merge-gate [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida db retire-legacy-ids
Collapse legacy origin spec_ids onto their agreed_ids. For each requirement where spec_id ≠
agreed_id (typically a legacy zero-padded origin id with a later-assigned short agreed id), set
spec_id := agreed_id and clear agreed_id. The on-disk YAML moves to the new sharded path;
relationships are unaffected (they use UUIDs). Run with --dry-run first to preview

Usage: aida db retire-legacy-ids [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --dry-run
          Show what would change without writing anything

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida db block
Manage pre-allocated agreed ID blocks for offline-safe trace comments

Usage: aida db block [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  claim   Claim a new block of agreed IDs for this node (requires network push)
  list    List all claimed blocks across all nodes
  status  Show blocks for the current node and their remaining capacity
  verify  Cross-check nodes.toml against blocks.yaml. Reports any block- owning node id missing from
          the registry and (under blocks-only policy) any registered node with no claimed block.
          Exits non-zero on inconsistency
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)

          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida db reconcile-status
Replay the Done → Completed auto-bump scan over a wider commit range than `aida pull` saw,
recovering specs that got stranded at Done. The pull-time auto-bump only scans commits the current
pull brings in; if a spec's YAML was unreadable at pull time, or the user pulled before flipping the
spec to Done, the bump silently misses and the spec is stuck without manual intervention

Usage: aida db reconcile-status [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --since <REF>
          Bound the scan range. Accepts a commit SHA, a tag, or any `git rev-parse`-able ref.
          Without --since, walks the most recent 200 commits on the default branch (an over-broad
          window is safe — only Done specs flip, so idempotent on already-Completed specs)

      --spec <SPEC-ID>
          Limit the replay to a single spec. Faster than the full scan when you know which spec is
          stuck. The same default- branch + status-Done guards apply

      --dry-run
          Show what would flip without writing anything. Pairs with `--since` / `--spec` for
          previewing a targeted replay

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida db check
Audit the store for consistency problems. Currently supports `--collisions` (two requirements
claiming the same short id, which the gate-time check prevents going forward but doesn't
retroactively detect)

Usage: aida db check [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --collisions
          Report requirements whose preferred display id (agreed_id when assigned, else spec_id)
          collides with another requirement's spec_id or agreed_id. Pre-existing collisions from
          before the gate-time check landed persist in the store and won't auto-clear

      --repair
          When used with `--collisions`, re-gate the later (higher position-encoded) claimant's
          agreed_id to the next free short id. The earlier claimant keeps the contested id. Without
          this flag, the command only reports; the operator decides which to keep

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida db migrate-related-edges
Repair custom edges that graph traversals do not follow.

Any edge stored as a custom type whose spelling resolves to a standard relationship type (for
example `related`, `depends-on`, `verified_by` or `replaced_by`) is rewritten: when the source
already has an edge of that standard type to the same target the custom edge is deleted, otherwise
it is converted in place. Other custom edge types (for example `implements` or a `sprint_*` label)
are left alone. Each changed spec is written with its own store commit, and the command refuses to
leave a spec holding two edges of the same type to one target. Running it again after a successful
run changes nothing.

Usage: aida db migrate-related-edges [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --dry-run
          Report the counts and the per-spec actions without writing anything

      --json
          Emit the report as JSON

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida cache
SQLite cache view commands (git-canonical mode only)

Usage: aida cache [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  rebuild  Force a full rebuild of the cache from the git store
  status   Show cache state (HEAD comparison, requirement count, last build time)
  refresh  Bring the cache current now; worker/scheduler forms drive the detached refresh protocol
  verify   Cross-check every cached status against the git store and report drift
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

===== aida record
Inspect or prune the durable per-spec processing record — the audit trail of what was done + why,
captured at completion time

Usage: aida record [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list   List the processing records for one spec (or every spec carrying any, when no id is given)
  prune  Trim processing records, keeping the spec. Records can be pruned later without losing the
         spec or its history. Propose-by-default — pass `--apply` to write
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when

===== aida record prune
Trim processing records, keeping the spec. Records can be pruned later without losing the spec or
its history. Propose-by-default — pass `--apply` to write

Usage: aida record prune [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --spec <SPEC>
          Restrict to one spec. Omit to sweep every spec

      --older-than <OLDER_THAN>
          Drop records older than this many days (e.g. `90`). When omitted, every record on the
          matched spec(s) is pruned

      --apply
          Actually write the prune. Without it, the command only reports what it would remove
          (propose-by-default)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida sandbox
Throwaway sandbox store for drain-testing / scenario play. Creates a discardable git-canonical store
under a temp dir; point `aida` at it with the printed `AIDA_STORE=...` export so drains and test
specs never touch the project's real store. `reset` re-seeds, `destroy` removes it

Usage: aida sandbox [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create   Create a fresh throwaway store and print the `AIDA_STORE=...` export to activate it.
           Idempotent unless `--force` (refuses to clobber a populated existing sandbox without it)
  reset    Wipe the sandbox store's contents and re-initialize it empty (or seeded with `--seed`).
           The directory itself is reused
  destroy  Delete the sandbox store directory entirely
  path     Print the path of the (default or `--path`) sandbox store and whether it exists. With
           `--export`, print the `AIDA_STORE=...` line to eval
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida sandbox create
Create a fresh throwaway store and print the `AIDA_STORE=...` export to activate it. Idempotent
unless `--force` (refuses to clobber a populated existing sandbox without it)

Usage: aida sandbox create [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --path <PATH>
          Where to create the sandbox store. Default: a stable per-user temp dir
          (`$TMPDIR/aida-sandbox-<user>`), so re-running points at the same playground

      --seed
          Seed a few curated scenario specs (a lifecycle walk + a blocked-by chain) so there's
          something to play with immediately

      --force
          Recreate even if the target already holds a populated sandbox store

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida sandbox path
Print the path of the (default or `--path`) sandbox store and whether it exists. With `--export`,
print the `AIDA_STORE=...` line to eval

Usage: aida sandbox path [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --path <PATH>
          Sandbox store dir (default: the per-user temp sandbox)

      --export
          Print a shell `export AIDA_STORE=...` line instead of the bare path

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida mailbox
Inter-agent mailbox: peer↔peer messaging (send / inbox / thread)

Usage: aida mailbox [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  latency  Show mailbox read latency for the active identity (or an explicit recipient)
  send     Send a message to another agent, or `--broadcast` to all
  inbox    Show an agent's inbox: messages addressed to it + broadcasts, oldest-first. Reading marks
           the inbox seen (clears unread); `--all` is the operator-wide read-only view across every
           agent
  notice   Ambient unread-mail notice for an agent's context: a capped, plain, role+user-scoped
           summary of unread messages, or nothing when the inbox is caught up. Never marks anything
           seen. The SessionStart / per-turn hook calls this; reading/acking stays the explicit
           `aida mailbox inbox`
  list     Operator overview: agents with mail waiting + unread / urgent-unread counts,
           most-recent-activity first
  read     Read one message by id or unique id prefix without changing unread state
  retract  Retract a sent message, leaving a withdrawn tombstone in mailbox views
  delete   Delete a sent message from mailbox views; records a marker so sync does not resurrect it
  archive  Archive read mailbox messages from the default inbox while preserving them for audit
  gc       Maintenance alias for `archive --older-than ... --read-only`
  thread   Show a full conversation thread, oldest-first
  sync     Digest the local layer into the git-canonical store (durable, replayable, shareable
           across clones) and commit it on the orphan branch. Idempotent
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida mailbox send
Send a message to another agent, or `--broadcast` to all

Usage: aida mailbox send [OPTIONS] [BODY]

Arguments:
  [BODY]
          The message body. For rich multi-line text, prefer --body-file or --stdin so the shell
          cannot expand backticks or `$()` before AIDA receives the text

Options:
      --to <TO>
          Recipient agent id (e.g. `codex`). Omit and pass `--broadcast` to reach everyone

      --broadcast
          Broadcast to every agent instead of a single recipient

      --subject <SUBJECT>
          Short subject shown by inbox and notice views

      --body-file <PATH>
          Read the message body from a file instead of a shell argument

      --stdin
          Read the message body from stdin instead of a shell argument

      --thread <THREAD>
          Attach to an existing thread (default: start a new thread)

      --in-reply-to <IN_REPLY_TO>
          Id of the message this replies to

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

      --from <FROM>
          Override the sender id (default: this shell's agent/user identity)

      --urgent
          Flag this as an urgent escalation ("stop"/heads-up) so it is surfaced out-of-band
          (statusline nag) instead of sitting unseen in a purely-chronological inbox. Lightweight:
          normal vs urgent only

      --intent <INTENT>
          How the recipient should treat this message: `fyi` (informational, surface only),
          `request` (needs a response), or `handoff` (work transfer). Default: fyi. Orthogonal to
          --urgent (loudness vs kind)
          
          [default: fyi]

      --relayed-from <SEAT>
          The seat whose claim this message relays. Use it when the body reproduces another seat's
          measurement, finding or argument; the reader then sees "via <you>, originally <seat>".
          Omit it for claims you verified yourself

      --allow-second-person
          Send a body that says "you"/"your" even though another recipient already received the same
          body (or this is a broadcast). By default that send is refused, because each reader takes
          the claim as addressed to itself

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida mailbox inbox
Show an agent's inbox: messages addressed to it + broadcasts, oldest-first. Reading marks the inbox
seen (clears unread); `--all` is the operator-wide read-only view across every agent

Usage: aida mailbox inbox [OPTIONS] [AGENT]

Arguments:
  [AGENT]
          Whose inbox (default: this shell's agent/user identity)

Options:
      --all
          Operator-wide view: every message across all agents, oldest-first, with its recipient
          shown. Read-only — does not mark anything seen

      --archived
          Show only archived messages. Read-only — does not mark anything seen

      --peek
          Show the inbox WITHOUT marking it seen (does not advance the read-watermark). Lets a hook
          or a glance surface mail without consuming the unread flag — reading/acking stays an
          explicit act (a plain `aida mailbox inbox`)

      --unread
          Show only UNREAD messages (newer than this inbox's read-watermark)

      --recent-read-tail <RECENT_READ_TAIL>
          Number of already-read messages to keep in the default newest-first inbox tail. Use 0 for
          unread-only default behavior
          
          [default: 5]

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida mailbox notice
Ambient unread-mail notice for an agent's context: a capped, plain, role+user-scoped summary of
unread messages, or nothing when the inbox is caught up. Never marks anything seen. The SessionStart
/ per-turn hook calls this; reading/acking stays the explicit `aida mailbox inbox`

Usage: aida mailbox notice [OPTIONS] [AGENT]

Arguments:
  [AGENT]
          Whose mail to summarize. Default: the union of this shell's agent/user identity and the
          session role (`AIDA_SESSION_ROLE`)

Options:
      --cap <CAP>
          Max messages to list before collapsing the rest into "+N more" (default: 5). Keeps the
          per-turn context injection bounded

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida mailbox list
Operator overview: agents with mail waiting + unread / urgent-unread counts, most-recent-activity
first

Options:
      --stranded
          Dead-letter view: only recipients that have UNREAD mail but match no known role or
          registered agent — misaddressed handoffs (a typo'd agent name, a wrong role) that no live
          identity will ever read

===== aida mailbox archive
Archive read mailbox messages from the default inbox while preserving them for audit

Usage: aida mailbox archive [OPTIONS] [MESSAGE_ID]

Arguments:
  [MESSAGE_ID]
          Message id to archive. Must already be read by the target inbox

Options:
      --older-than <OLDER_THAN>
          Sweep read mail older than this point: a relative duration (`30d`, `12h`, `2w`, or `24
          hours ago`), an ISO date (`2026-05-01`, local midnight), a zone-less ISO datetime (local
          time), or RFC3339

      --read-only
          Required with --older-than; documents that unread mail is never touched

      --agent <AGENT>
          Whose read-watermark gates archive safety (default: current inbox identities)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida mailbox gc
Maintenance alias for `archive --older-than ... --read-only`

Usage: aida mailbox gc [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --older-than <OLDER_THAN>
          Sweep read mail older than this point (default: 30d). Same forms as `aida mail archive
          --older-than`
          
          [default: 30d]

      --agent <AGENT>
          Whose read-watermark gates archive safety (default: current inbox identities)

      --phantoms
          Instead of the age sweep, archive mail addressed to phantom recipients (flags, numbers,
          spec IDs, commit SHAs, unknown @mention handles) and re-address whitespace-padded
          recipients, printing each message it touches

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida node
Manage per-clone node identity (acquire/release node ids in the shared registry, list registered
clones). Each clone of an AIDA project gets a unique node id; that id is the namespace for
node-aware spec ids (e.g. `FR-<node>-<NNN>`) until the merge gate promotes them to short agreed-ids

Usage: aida node [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list       List all nodes registered in the shared registry. The current node (the one whose
             `.aida/node.toml` matches an entry) is marked with `*`
  show       Show details for a single node. With no id, defaults to the current node (read from
             `.aida/node.toml`)
  acquire    Acquire a node id for this clone. Performs a CAS push loop on the shared registry to
             claim the next sequential id, then writes the per-clone identity file at
             `.aida-store/.aida/node.toml`. Defaults pull `git config user.email` for the email
             stamp and the system hostname for the hostname stamp
  set-owner  Backfill the owner ($USER string) on an existing node entry in the shared registry,
             then push (CAS). If the id is the CURRENT node, the local `.aida/node.toml` is updated
             too. Errors clearly if the id is absent. For legacy nodes that predate the owner/name
             identity fields
  set-name   Backfill the friendly name on an existing node entry in the shared registry, then push
             (CAS). If the id is the CURRENT node, the local `.aida/node.toml` is updated too.
             Errors clearly if the id is absent
  release    Remove a node entry from the shared registry. Does not invalidate any IDs already
             issued by that node. The node id is not reused
  team       List the team: every registered node/clone sharing this store, with each member's role.
             Identity introspection under the `node` namespace. Equivalent to the top-level `aida
             team` (kept visible because the multi-clone harness invokes it); with a subcommand,
             manage per-user roles (`set-role`, `my-role`)
  whoami     Print the caller identity AIDA resolved — role, agent-type, agent-name, user-id,
             headless flag, ai-tool, and active session/scope. Read-only. Identity introspection
             under the `node` namespace; equivalent to the hidden top-level `aida whoami`
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida node acquire
Acquire a node id for this clone. Performs a CAS push loop on the shared registry to claim the next
sequential id, then writes the per-clone identity file at `.aida-store/.aida/node.toml`. Defaults
pull `git config user.email` for the email stamp and the system hostname for the hostname stamp

Usage: aida node acquire [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --id <ID>
          Claim a specific node id (must be free in the registry). Accepted as a string — `"JM"` or
          `"1"` alike

      --hostname <HOSTNAME>
          Override the hostname stamp (default: system hostname)

      --email <EMAIL>
          Override the email stamp (default: `git config user.email`)

      --node-name <NAME>
          Friendly name for this node, recorded alongside the node id in the shared roster (`aida
          team`). Defaults to `<host>-<user>-<seq>` (e.g. `imac-joe-1`). At a TTY with no flag you
          are prompted with the default pre-filled; non-interactive use takes the default silently

      --force
          Re-acquire even if `.aida/node.toml` already exists (default: refuse)

      --yes
          On collision, accept the suggested numeric-suffix fallback without prompting (e.g., `JM`
          taken → silently use `JM2`). Implies non- interactive mode

      --hijack <ID>
          Re-claim an already-registered node id (the shared registry entry gets re-attributed to
          this clone). When the previous clone is reachable on this host, drops a HIJACKED.toml
          marker inside its `.aida-store/.aida/` so the user sees a warning the next time they run
          `aida` there. Mutually exclusive with `--id`

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

      --remote-only
          Backfill a node entry into the shared registry for some OTHER (typically legacy) clone,
          then push — WITHOUT touching this clone's own identity. The running clone keeps its
          `.aida/node.toml` untouched and no blocks are allocated. Requires explicit `--id`,
          `--hostname`, and `--email` (nothing is inferred from the local environment, since the
          entry is not about this clone). Mutually exclusive with `--hijack` and `--force`

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida node team
List the team: every registered node/clone sharing this store, with each member's role. Identity
introspection under the `node` namespace. Equivalent to the top-level `aida team` (kept visible

Usage: aida node team [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  set-role       Set a user's durable team role in the roster (`registry/team.toml`, CAS push-wins).
                 A rostered role is the user's effective role even with no `AIDA_SESSION_ROLE` set,

  my-role        Show YOUR effective role: the roster role for your user id if present, else

  unset-role     Remove a user's entry from the roster (`registry/team.toml`, CAS push). A friendly
                 no-op if the user isn't present. Use this to clean stray / duplicate keys — e.g. an
                 orphaned integer key left by an older roster
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

===== aida status
Show "where am I right now" — unified view of session, branch, PR/CI, queue, cache, and project
state. Spiritual cousin of `git status`: one screen, no flag-guessing.

Default sections (each graceful-degrades when its data isn't available): Session  — active lease
covering cwd: id, scope, role, worktree, age Branch   — current branch, dirty state, ahead/behind
origin PR / CI  — open PR for the branch + check rollup (via `gh`) Queue    — top items routed to
the active role + total count Cache    — orphan-store cache freshness Project  — storage mode,
requirement counts (existing view)

With a SPEC argument (`aida status <spec>`), switch to the per-spec liveness view: the spec's
lifecycle status plus a LIVENESS section answering "is a live session actually working this, or is
the In-Progress flag orphaned?". For a spec-scoped session lease it shows the session id, role,
worktree, started-at, elapsed, and a verdict: live (the holder process is alive) vs STALE (no live
process — the flag is orphaned). An In-Progress spec with no spec-scoped lease reads flag-only (the
status is not liveness-backed).

Usage: aida status [OPTIONS] [SPEC]

Arguments:
  [SPEC]
          Optional spec id (SPEC-ID / agreed id). When given, show the per-spec liveness view
          (status + live/STALE/flag-only verdict) instead of the project-wide "where am I" snapshot

Options:
      --idle-minutes <IDLE_MINUTES>
          With a SPEC argument: minutes of idle a spec-scoped lease may sit with a live process but
          no spec movement before it is reported as STALLED rather than live. Default 180 (3h).
          Ignored without a SPEC
          
          [default: 180]

      --no-dev-context
          Suppress the AIDA-development-context section even when running inside the aida repo

      --short
          One-line summary (spiritual cousin of `aida statusline`). Suppresses every section except
          a compact role/scope/branch readout

      --json
          Machine-readable JSON output. Sections that fail (gh unavailable, no session, etc.) appear
          as `null` so consumers can detect "section absent" without parsing prose. Same document as
          `--format json`.
          
          With a SPEC argument the document is the per-spec liveness view: `spec`, `status`,
          `status_lens`, `in_progress`, `liveness` (`live` | `stale` | `flag-only` | `no-session` —
          `flag-only` stays distinct from `live`/`stale`, never collapsed into either), `live`
          (bool), `active_pid`, `worktree`, `idle_secs`, `idle_stalled`, `session`
          (session_id/scope/role/worktree/branch/ started_at/elapsed_secs/pid, or `null`), `drain`
          (phase/round/ orchestrator_pid when a live drain owns the spec, else `null`), and `parked`
          (source: `orchestrator` | `punt`, plus phase/kind/cause/detail/hint for an orchestrator
          shelving or category/detail/lean for an agent punt; `null` when not parked).

      --queue
          Focus on the queue section only — skip everything else

      --ci
          Focus on the PR / CI section only — skip everything else

      --no-ci
          Skip the gh-backed PR / CI lookup (offline / fast path). The PR/CI section is omitted from
          text output and reported as `null` in `--json`

      --cleanup
          Focus on the cleanup section only — print just "Needs attention" (sticky In-Progress
          specs, missed auto-bumps, dormant leases, stale-on-merged reviewer leases, branches ahead
          with no PR, worktrees with uncommitted work, orphan project dirs, open PRs awaiting
          merge). Default `aida status` adds a one-line summary at the bottom when the section is
          non-empty.
          
          This is a READ-ONLY view — it surfaces what needs cleanup, it does not change anything. To
          actually fix the auto-healable items, run `aida doctor heal` (or `aida doctor check` to
          diagnose first). Think of it as glance (status --cleanup) → fix (doctor heal).

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

      --activity
          Focus on live advisor/external activity recorded in `.aida/advisor-activity.jsonl`.
          
          This is a READ-ONLY view. Default `aida status` shows a short recent footer when activity
          exists; pass `--activity` for the full filtered feed.

      --since <SINCE>
          With `--activity`, only show events after this point: a relative duration (`30m`, `12h`,
          `2d`, `2w`, or `24 hours ago`), an ISO date (`2026-05-01`, local midnight), a zone-less
          ISO datetime (`2026-05-01T10:00`, local time), or an RFC3339 timestamp

      --awaiting
          Focus on the "Awaiting you" section only — every human-gate item (mergeable PRs with no
          pending CI / requested changes, unacked briefs, findings awaiting triage, NeedsAttention
          escalations). On default `aida status` this section also leads the report

      --verbose
          With `--cleanup`: list every item per category instead of the first 3. With `--awaiting`
          (or on default status): lift the 5-item cap on the "Awaiting you" section to show every
          item

      --no-hygiene
          Suppress the AIDA doctor "Hygiene" section entirely

      --all
          Show the full fleet roster: reveal stale (dead-PID) agents the default view hides behind a
          footer count, and list every worktree instead of collapsing a large roster to a one-line
          summary. By default `aida status` reflects LIVE reality and points at `aida doctor heal` /
          `aida session gc` to reap the abandoned ones

      --stale
          Reveal only the stale (dead-PID) agents the default "Active agents" headline hides — the
          narrow form of `--all` (worktrees stay summarized)

      --full
          Reproduce the exhaustive dump: expand every section the terse default collapses to a
          one-line summary (open-PR roster, recently merged, inferred remote activity, cross-clone
          coordination, the recent-activity feed, the per-status requirement breakdown, and the
          AIDA-dev-context block). By default `aida status` leads with the answer — session / branch
          / PR / queue / what-needs-you — and folds the long-tail rosters behind one-liners so the
          orientation command fits roughly one screen. `--all` implies `--full` (and also reveals
          the fleet roster). Use `--full` when you want the full picture without the stale-agent /
          worktree expansion `--all` adds

      --no-focus
          Ignore the active focus for this snapshot — drop the focus banner. No-op when no focus is
          set. (`aida status --all` is the fleet roster, a different axis, so focus has its own
          escape here.)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida awaiting
The unified coordination inbox — every channel where YOU are the gate, in ONE place: mergeable PRs,
unacked briefs, findings awaiting triage, reviewer verdicts, NeedsAttention escalations, unread
mail, AND pending worker directives. The same "Awaiting you" report that leads `aida status`,
promoted to a first-class command so the whole coordination inbox is a can't-miss signal — not just
mail (which had its own per-turn hook while everything else stayed invisible mid-session).

`--notice` renders the COMPACT one-line form the per-turn hook injects (silent when nothing awaits).
That path is cache/local-backed and makes NO network call — PRs (the one gh-backed channel) are
omitted from the line; run the bare command to include them.

Usage: aida awaiting [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --notice
          Compact one-line summary spanning every channel, for the per-turn hook. SILENT when
          nothing awaits. Cache/local-backed, no network (PRs are omitted from this line — run bare
          `aida awaiting` for them)

      --json
          Machine-readable JSON of the full report (same shape as `aida status --awaiting --json`)

  -v, --verbose
          Lift the 5-item cap and show every item

      --no-ci
          Skip the gh-backed PR lookup (offline / fast path). Implied by `--notice`

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)

===== aida ps
The global running-work table — one row per active session/agent across the project (the
`ps`/`docker ps` of AIDA work). Companion to `aida status <spec>` (per-spec): where that answers "is
THIS spec liveness-backed?", `aida ps` answers "what is genuinely running on my machine right now,
and what only CLAIMS to be?".

Each session row shows: session id, spec (scope), role, worktree, pid, started, ELAPSED, and a
liveness verdict reusing the same machinery `aida status <spec>` and `aida session leases` use (live
/ dormant / STALE).

It ALSO surfaces ORPHANED In-Progress specs — specs at status In-Progress with NO spec-scoped lease
backing them (the flag-only case) — so a crashed or never-started session can't hide behind a status
flag. AIDA-launched work (`aida queue work` / `aida agent new`) gets spec-scoped leases (the rich,
spec-linked rows); advisor Agent-tool fan-outs take generic `harness-worktree` leases (shown by
session/worktree, spec unknown).

Usage: aida ps [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json
          Machine-readable JSON output: `{ sessions: [...], orphaned: [...] }`

      --all
          Include STALE (dead-pid / leaked) session rows that the default view folds behind a footer
          count

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida merge-hold
Inspect and clear supervised merge-hold markers (`.aida/merge-holds/`).

A hold marker keeps a PR held for human/advisor review — it fails the merge-hold-gate required check
so the PR cannot be auto-merged. AIDA merge paths (`aida pr ship`, the autonomous drain) clear the
marker automatically when they merge; this is the manual surface for the case they cannot see — a PR
merged directly (a raw `gh pr merge`) leaves a phantom marker behind. `list` shows every marker and
flags the ones whose PR has already merged as stale; `clear` removes them.

Usage: aida merge-hold [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  auto-release  Release eligible Rework-only holds using a fresh recorded approval. Sensitive or
                composed holds still require a human clear
  labels        Inspect or provision the three repository-level merge-hold label definitions
  list          List every active merge-hold: marker-backed holds AND holds that exist only as the
                `aida:merge-hold` label (shown as `label-only (no marker)`). Each row is the held PR
                + the hold reason. A marker whose PR merged or closed without merging is flagged
                stale; a marker whose stated premise has moved (the PR head passed the commit it
                cites, or a rework hold's verdict is now approved or closed) is flagged `premise
                stale` for a human to judge — nothing is cleared automatically
  add           Place a supervised merge-hold by hand: write the marker file AND mirror the
                `aida:merge-hold` label, so a PR you hold outside a drain releases through the same
                `aida merge-hold clear <pr>` path (a label applied by hand alone leaves the required
                check red with nothing to release). Refuses when the PR already has a marker unless
                `--replace` is given; `aida merge-hold list --fix` re-applies a missing label
                without touching the marker
  clear         Clear a merge-hold: remove the marker file and drop the `aida:merge-hold` label,
                releasing the PR for merge. A hold that exists only as the label is cleared the same
                way and the clearance recorded. Give a PR number, or `--stale` to sweep every marker
                whose PR can never merge (merged, or closed without merging)
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida merge-hold list
List every active merge-hold: marker-backed holds AND holds that exist only as the `aida:merge-hold`
