          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida worktree pool
Manage the warm-pool of recycled worktrees — kept warm (reset-not-delete on hand-back) so build
caches survive across fan-outs. Dissolves the cargo-cache poison and branch-stacking hazards of
destroy-and-recreate

Usage: aida worktree pool [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status   Show every pooled worktree with its live state (available / in-use / leased / dirty /
           destroying) and current HEAD. Read-only
  acquire  Acquire a worktree from the pool: reuse an idle warm tree (reset to a clean detached
           base) or create a new one up to the cap. Prints the path
  return   Return a worktree to the pool: reset it to a clean detached base and mark it idle. The
           directory PERSISTS (the warm cache is kept). Defaults to the pool tree containing the
           current directory
  adopt    Register EXISTING worktrees into the warm-pool — the migration path for sibling worktrees
           created before the pool existed. DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT: pass `--no-dry-run` to write the
           registry. Never touches a worktree (no reset, no checkout, no removal) and is safe to
           re-run. A tree that still carries uncommitted or unmerged work needs `--include-unlanded`
           and is registered as a RESERVATION, so it is never handed out until you release it with
           `pool return`
  destroy  Tear down pool worktrees. DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT — pass `--no-dry-run` to actually remove.
           Each tree is classified by risk; only `disposable` trees are removed unless you opt into
           a riskier class with one `--include-*` flag. This is the ONLY path that deletes a
           directory
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Usage: aida worktree pool destroy [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

  [PATHS]...
          Specific worktree path(s) to destroy. Omit with `--all` for a bulk sweep (in which
          `--include-leased` is ignored as a safety stop)

Options:
      --all
          Target every pooled worktree

      --no-dry-run
          Actually remove (the default is a preview)

      --include-unlanded
          Allow removing dirty / unmerged / unverified trees (uncommitted or unlanded work is
          patch-salvaged first)

      --include-in-use
          Allow removing a tree with a live owner process

      --include-leased
          Allow removing a durably-leased tree — honored only when the exact path is named, never in
          a `--all` sweep

      --json
          Emit JSON instead of the human report

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =

===== aida intent
Show the AI-generated plain-terms comprehension of WHY a spec exists — its intent, distilled from
the spec + its graph neighborhood. Distinct from `aida why` (a deterministic state classifier): this
is a cached, drift-stamped LLM synthesis. Generated on first call (or `--refresh`), printed from
cache thereafter; a STALE marker shows when the neighborhood drifted since generation

Usage: aida intent [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>
          The SPEC-ID to comprehend (any story/task/bug/feature id)

Options:
      --audience <AUDIENCE>
          Which register to print: `layman` (prose for a human skimmer) or `llm` (denser/structured,
          for an agent loading the spec)
          
          [default: layman]
          [possible values: layman, llm]

      --refresh
          Force regeneration even if a cached comprehension exists and is fresh

      --json
          Machine-readable JSON (`{spec, audience, comprehension, generated_at, model, stale}`)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida dev
AIDA-developer-only commands: activate the in-repo dev binary, run dev servers, install shell
helpers. End users don't need these

Usage: aida dev [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  activate    Emit shell code that prepends the in-repo build dir to PATH. Use as: `eval "$(aida dev
              activate)"`. By default the release build (`target/release/aida`) is activated — pass
              `debug` / `release` (or `--debug` / `--release`) to PIN a specific profile across
              subsequent re-activations, or `auto` (`--auto`) to pin freshest-wins selection (newest
              SHA-matched of debug vs release, re-picked on every activate)
  build       Build, smoke-test and promote the live dev binary. The one build command: an
              incremental `--profile agent` workspace build, then a smoke test of the new `aida` /
              `aida-server`, then an atomic promote into the live directory (default
              `~/.local/share/aida/live`, outside target/), keeping the previous pair in
              `live/prev/`. Promotes only from the primary checkout on a clean `main` that matches
              `origin/main` (the local remote-tracking ref; it does not fetch, so run `git fetch`
              first); in a worktree it builds and smoke-tests only
  rollback    Swap the previous live binaries (`live/prev/`) back in, in one step. Running it again
              rolls forward. Refuses while a live drain wave is pinned to the live binary unless
              --after-wave or --force
  deactivate  Emit shell code that undoes a previous `aida dev activate`. Use as: `eval "$(aida dev
              deactivate)"`
  serve       Run aida-server (REST/gRPC) and the React dev server (vite) in the foreground. Ctrl+C
              stops both. Defaults to serving the current project's store; React dev server only
              starts when run from the AIDA repo (since aida-web-react/ lives there)
  status      Show current dev-activation state: is AIDA_DEV_ACTIVE set, what binary is being used,
              when was it built, what's the AIDA repo path
  ps1         Print the compact PS1 staleness marker for the active dev binary
  shell-init  Print shell helper functions (aida-on, aida-off) suitable for pasting into ~/.bashrc
              or ~/.zshrc. Pass --install to append them directly
  release     One-command release: bump the version through a release PR, tag the merged commit and
              push the tag (via scripts/release.sh), wait for the GitHub Actions workflow to publish
              binary tarballs, then upgrade your sibling installs to the new version. Default bump:
              patch
  patch       Alias for `aida dev release patch` — the most common case
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida dev activate
Emit shell code that prepends the in-repo build dir to PATH. Use as: `eval "$(aida dev activate)"`.
By default the release build (`target/release/aida`) is activated — pass `debug` / `release` (or
`--debug` / `--release`) to PIN a specific profile across subsequent re-activations, or `auto`
(`--auto`) to pin freshest-wins selection (newest SHA-matched of debug vs release, re-picked on
every activate)

Usage: aida dev activate [OPTIONS] [PROFILE]

Arguments:
  [PROFILE]
          Profile shortcut: `debug`, `release`, or `auto` (positional). Equivalent to `--debug` /
          `--release` / `--auto`. Pins for subsequent re-activations
          
          [possible values: debug, release, auto]

Options:
      --repo <REPO>
          Override the AIDA repo path (defaults to current directory if it looks like the aida repo,
          or $AIDA_DEV_REPO if set)

      --debug
          Pin to the debug build (target/debug). Sticky — subsequent plain `aida dev activate`
          invocations honor the pin until you pass --auto or --release

      --release
          Pin to the release build (target/release). Sticky. Also the default when nothing is pinned

      --auto
          Pin freshest-wins selection: the newest SHA-matched of debug/release is re-picked on every
          activate. Sticky until you pin debug or release

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida dev build
Build, smoke-test and promote the live dev binary. The one build command: an incremental `--profile
agent` workspace build, then a smoke test of the new `aida` / `aida-server`, then an atomic promote
into the live directory (default `~/.local/share/aida/live`, outside target/), keeping the previous
pair in `live/prev/`. Promotes only from the primary checkout on a clean `main` that matches
`origin/main` (the local remote-tracking ref; it does not fetch, so run `git fetch` first); in a
worktree it builds and smoke-tests only

Usage: aida dev build [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --clean[=<CLEAN>]
          Clear the incremental cache first. Bare `--clean` deletes only `target/agent/incremental`
          (keeps compiled dependencies); `--clean=full` runs `cargo clean --profile agent`

          Possible values:
          - incremental: Delete only `target/agent/incremental`; keep compiled dependencies
          - full:        Run `cargo clean --profile agent`

      --no-promote
          Build and smoke-test only; never promote

      --allow-dirty
          Promote even when the checkout is dirty, off `main`, or not at `origin/main` (`aida dev
          status` then shows the dirty SHA)

      --install-links
          Point `~/.local/bin/aida` and `~/.local/bin/aida-server` at the live directory, showing
          anything it replaces first

      --yes
          With --install-links: replace existing files/links without asking (required when stdin is
          not a terminal)

      --after-wave
          Wait for a live drain wave pinned to the current binary to finish instead of refusing

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida driver
Register, refresh, deregister and list drivers — long-running relays, drains and agents that work
in-progress specs. `aida ps` and `aida list` show the driver beside each in-progress spec's status.
Operator/developer surface

Usage: aida driver [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  register    Register (or refresh the heartbeat of) a driver. The record stays live for as long as
              the registered pid is alive; it reads as not live once that process exits. Pass
              `--ttl` to also expire it when the heartbeat is not refreshed within that many seconds
  deregister  Remove the driver record registered under this kind and id. There is no ownership
              check: any caller can remove any record by name
  list        List registered drivers and whether each is live
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida driver register
Register (or refresh the heartbeat of) a driver. The record stays live for as long as the registered
pid is alive; it reads as not live once that process exits. Pass `--ttl` to also expire it when the
heartbeat is not refreshed within that many seconds

Usage: aida driver register [OPTIONS] --run <RUN>

Options:
      --kind <KIND>
          Driver kind: relay, drain or agent
          
          [default: relay]

      --run <RUN>
          The driver's id (a relay run id, a drain pid, an agent session)

      --tag <TAG>
          Tag selector the driver works through, e.g. `batch:next`. In-progress specs carrying this
          tag resolve to this driver

      --pid <PID>
          The driver's own long-lived process id. Pass `--pid "$$"` from the driver's loop: the
          parent of `aida` is a throwaway subshell when called from `$(...)` or a pipe. Required for
          relays; other kinds fall back to the parent process. The pid must be running unless
          `--ttl` is given

      --seat <SEAT>
          Seat the driver occupies, if any

      --handoff <HANDOFF>
          Path to the driver's handoff/notes file, if any

      --ttl <TTL>
          Heartbeat TTL in seconds. When set, the record also stops being live if `register` is not
          re-run within this window. Default: no heartbeat expiry (liveness follows the pid alone)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

      --json
          Machine-readable JSON

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

          [default: relay]

      --format <FORMAT>

===== aida doctor
Diagnose and heal AIDA multi-agent state drift. Report-only by design: exit 0 means the scan RAN,
not that it found nothing — findings print as text/JSON either way. A caller that needs a pass/fail
signal (e.g. a CI gate or scheduled job) opts in with `doctor check <category> --fail-on-findings`,
which exits non-zero only when that one category has findings

Usage: aida doctor [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  shell-substitution-holes  Find prose that may have lost backticked text to shell command
                            substitution. Reports only; candidates require human inspection
  check                     Focused multi-agent drift diagnostic for one category
  heal                      Focused multi-agent drift heal for one category
  migrate-counter-scope     Migrate this project from per-type counters (each type counts
                            independently — every type starts back at 1) to a single global counter
                            (one shared sequence — IDs increment across types). Allocates a new `*`
                            block above the existing per-type blocks' max range_end, marks per-type
                            blocks as exhausted, sets `[id_format] counter_scope = "global"`.
                            Existing requirement spec_ids stay unchanged — only newly-added reqs use
                            the global counter
  repair-stale-blocks       Find and tombstone blocks whose `node_id` isn't in nodes.toml (orphaned
                            from a clone that never registered, or from a pre-multi-node store). The
                            block range stays reserved so other clones don't reallocate over it;
                            `next` is bumped past `range_end` so the dispenser skips it
  scrub-collisions          Detect duplicate spec_ids in the orphan store — multiple YAMLs claiming
                            the same id (legacy leftovers, imports gone wrong). Reports only; v1
                            doesn't auto-renumber because that would orphan trace comments and
                            commit refs
  validate-trace-comments   Walk source files under the project root for AIDA trace annotations and
                            verify each spec_id resolves to an existing requirement. Catches dead
                            trace comments left behind after a req got deleted, or simple typos.
                            Default is read-only; pass `--strip-dangling` to remove markers pointing
                            at unknown spec_ids (whole comment line deleted if the trace was its
                            only content; otherwise just the trace fragment is excised)
  convention-check          Check that STORY / BUG descriptions contain a recognized acceptance
                            heading (`## Acceptance`, `## Verify`, `## Tests`, `## Test cases`, `##
                            Verification` — case-insensitive). Surfaced by the review-prompt
                            generator: missing sections produce a placeholder downstream, this lint
                            catches them at write-time. Exits non-zero if any STORY/BUG is missing a
                            section
  help                      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --heal
          Apply safe fixes after scanning. Without this, doctor is read-only

  -y, --yes
          Skip per-category confirmation prompts while healing

      --category <CATEGORY>
          Restrict scan/heal to one category

      --json
          Emit machine-readable JSON

      --force
          Permit riskier destructive fixes such as branch deletion

      --all
          Show older completed-without-commit findings individually

      --since <DATE_OR_REF>
          Exempt specs completed before this point from the completed-without-commit integrity
          check: a relative duration (`30d`, `2w`, `24 hours ago`), an ISO date (local midnight), a
          zone-less ISO datetime (local time), RFC3339, or else a git ref/tag whose commit date is
          the cutoff. An invalid value is an error. Quiets noise on legacy history predating trace
          conventions. Falls back to the AIDA_DOCTOR_COMPLETED_SINCE env var

      --fix-sandbox
          Print the guided, copy-pasteable steps to bring the OS sandbox (bubblewrap
          write-confinement) up on this host: detect the current state, the exact sysctl to persist
          if the kernel blocks unprivileged user namespaces, how to opt in, and the verify command.
          Prints the sequence — sudo steps are clearly marked "run this yourself"; it never silently
          runs sudo. Runs the non-sudo availability re-probe as a smoke check

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

      --contradictions
          Run a store-wide semantic contradiction sweep combining mechanical joins in Rust with Jev
          System One semantic choice queries

      --contradictions-limit <N>
          Maximum contradiction findings to print per page. The default is deliberately bounded; use
          --contradictions-offset to continue or --all to request the complete scan
          
          [default: 25]

      --contradictions-offset <N>
          Zero-based offset into the deterministically ordered contradiction findings. Ignored with
          --all
          
          [default: 0]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida doctor verify-relationships
Walk every requirement's `relationships` array and verify each `target_id` resolves to an existing
requirement UUID. Catches dangling references from deleted reqs, bad imports, or hand-edits. With
--repair, strips dangling entries

Usage: aida doctor verify-relationships [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --repair
          Strip dangling references in-place. Without this flag, the command reports only

  -y, --yes
          Skip the y/N confirmation when --repair would write

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida doctor validate-trace-comments
Walk source files under the project root for AIDA trace annotations and verify each spec_id resolves
to an existing requirement. Catches dead trace comments left behind after a req got deleted, or
simple typos. Default is read-only; pass `--strip-dangling` to remove markers pointing at unknown
spec_ids (whole comment line deleted if the trace was its only content; otherwise just the trace
fragment is excised)

Usage: aida doctor validate-trace-comments [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --strip-dangling
          Rewrite source files to remove dangling AIDA trace annotations. Lossy — comments around
          the marker are preserved, but the pointer itself is gone

      --dry-run
          Print what would change without writing

  -y, --yes
          Skip the y/N confirmation when --strip-dangling would write

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida doctor fsck
Run every diagnostic in sequence and print a unified report. Composes `aida db block verify`,
repair-stale-blocks --dry-run, scrub-collisions, verify-relationships, validate-trace-comments, plus
a few smaller checks. Exits non-zero if any check found a problem

Usage: aida doctor fsck [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida doctor convention-check
Check that STORY / BUG descriptions contain a recognized acceptance heading (`## Acceptance`, `##
Verify`, `## Tests`, `## Test cases`, `## Verification` — case-insensitive). Surfaced by the
review-prompt generator: missing sections produce a placeholder downstream, this lint catches them
at write-time. Exits non-zero if any STORY/BUG is missing a section

Usage: aida doctor convention-check [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -q, --quiet
          Quiet mode — print only the summary line, omit per-spec rows

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida store
Inspect and align the orphan-store SHA against code commits. Pairs with the prepare-commit-msg hook
(`aida-store-pair.sh`) that pins the store SHA into every code commit's trailer via an `Aida-Store:
<sha>` line

Usage: aida store [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status         Show the relationship between the current code commit and the orphan store: which
                 store SHA the code was paired with at commit time, what the store HEAD is now,
                 drift in commits between them
  install-hook   Install the prepare-commit-msg hook (`aida-store-pair.sh`) into `.git/hooks/`.
                 Idempotent — safe to re-run. New projects get this hook from `aida init`
                 automatically; this command exists for retrofitting an existing project
  compact        Deep-repack the orphan store git repo to relieve the substrate tax of a long,
                 never-compacted history. The bare command runs an aggressive `git gc` — safe +
                 non-destructive: no history is rewritten, `aida history` is unaffected, no
                 force-push needed. `gc` is an alias
  scrub-preview  Preview the identity this machine will WRITE to the shared store — hostname + git
                 email, and how the configured redaction (`[node] public_hostname` / `public_email`
                 in `~/.aida/config.toml`) rewrites them. Read-only; verify up front, before your
                 first push, that no raw corporate identity will land in a public-mirrored store
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida store compact
Deep-repack the orphan store git repo to relieve the substrate tax of a long, never-compacted
history. The bare command runs an aggressive `git gc` — safe + non-destructive: no history is
rewritten, `aida history` is unaffected, no force-push needed. `gc` is an alias

Usage: aida store compact [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --squash
          DESTRUCTIVE opt-in: rewrite the orphan-store history to a single snapshot commit. Rewrites
          the branch (breaks the full `aida history events` timeline — preserved only via the backup
          ref) and needs a coordinated force-push every clone must re-sync. Never runs
          automatically. Without `--yes` it only PRINTS the plan

      --yes
          Required to actually perform a `--squash` rewrite. Without it, `--squash` prints exactly
          what it would do and exits without touching the store

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida schedule
Per-seat job registry: substrate jobs run by the tick, seat jobs delivered to whoever holds the seat
(alias: `aida cron`)

Usage: aida schedule [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  tick               Evaluate every enabled job: run due substrate jobs, mark due seat jobs
  run                Force one job now (substrate: execute; seat: print its prompt), or every
                     enabled substrate job
  status             Show every configured job with kind, seats, schedule, status, last run, next
                     due — plus legacy `.aida/schedules.toml` cadence entries
  list               List the merged registry (project + global) with source layer and last reporter
  due                What is due right now: seat jobs for a seat (or every seat), plus due substrate
                     jobs when no seat filter is given
  done               Report a seat job as done: ledgers who/when on the aida-store branch and clears
                     the due flag
  emit-cron          Print crontab lines for enabled substrate jobs with an `every`
  install-cron       Install the crontab entry that drives `aida schedule tick` for this repo every
                     15 minutes (Linux/macOS only; idempotent — safe to re-run). This is what `aida
                     init`'s TTY prompt calls, and the fix hint `aida doctor` prints when it finds
                     registered jobs but no installed driver
  uninstall-cron     Remove this repo's crontab entry installed by `install-cron` (or the `aida
                     init` prompt). Idempotent — a no-op when nothing is installed; never touches
                     another repo's entry
  install-systemd    Install a systemd user timer that runs `aida schedule tick` for this repo
                     (Linux only; idempotent — safe to re-run, and it repairs an older unit). The
                     timer is enabled and verified first; only then is this repo's crontab entry
                     removed. Needs a human at an interactive terminal and an explicit yes.
                     `install-cron` likewise removes this timer
  uninstall-systemd  Disable and delete this repo's systemd user timer. Only the timer is disabled:
                     a tick already running finishes. Unit files that aida did not write are left
                     alone. Idempotent
  help               Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida role
Manage personas / hats — persistent named contexts that resume across shells. `aida role enter
<name>` switches; `aida role list` shows what's defined for this project. State at `.aida/roles/`

Usage: aida role [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  enter     Enter (resume) an existing role. With no name on an interactive terminal, shows a picker
            of the project's roles; non-interactively it errors. Outputs shell code that must run in
            the calling shell: raw binary: `eval "$(aida role enter advisor)"` via the shell helper
            (`aida dev shell-init`): just `aida role enter advisor` The helper auto-evals it, so the
            bare form is correct there
  add       Add a new role, then enter it. Errors if the name already exists (use `aida role enter`
            to resume an existing one)
  list      List all roles for this project (and any global roles), sorted by last activity. Active
            role marked with `*`
  show      Show details for one role (defaults to the active role if any)
  active    Print the active role's name and exit, or exit 1 with empty stdout when no role is
            active. Resolves the validated grant — no project-store load. Shell-friendly counterpart
            to `git branch --show-current`
  current   Print the active role's name on stdout (empty line when no role is active) and exit 0
            either way. With `--check`, exit 1 instead when no role is active (still printing the
            name when one is). Resolves the validated grant — no project-store load.
            Scripting-friendly surface for agents without direct env access
  expiry    Report how close this session's seat grant is to expiry. By default prints a one-line
            warning on stdout when the grant expires within `--warn-within` (or has expired), and
            nothing otherwise; always exits 0. With `--refuse-within`, prints the refusal on stderr
            and exits 3 when less than that is left: a relay runs it before launching each seat
            session; it also exits 3 when `AIDA_SESSION_GRANT` is set but its grant can't be used
            (missing, malformed, or revoked). No grant at all, or an implementer grant, is never
            refused
  end       Deactivate the current role (state preserved). Outputs shell code: `eval "$(aida role
            end)"`
  delete    Delete a role's state file permanently. Confirms before deleting unless --yes is passed
  scaffold  Install a starter set of global roles (implementer, product, advisor, reviewer,
            integrator) at ~/.aida/roles/. Idempotent — skips any that already exist; safe to
            re-run. (`architect` / `triage` are opt-in via `aida role add`.)
  scope     Manage per-role scope filters. Scope filters are auto-applied to `aida list` and `aida
            queue list/next` while the role is active — e.g. set `--tags inbox --status draft` on
            the `triage` role to always see just the inbox-tagged drafts when wearing that hat.
            Override on a single command with explicit --tags/--status flags or --no-scope
  prompt    Manage the per-role Claude Code system-prompt addendum. The text is injected into
            Claude's context at session start via the aida-role-context.sh hook when this role is
            active
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida role enter
Enter (resume) an existing role. With no name on an interactive terminal, shows a picker of the
project's roles; non-interactively it errors. Outputs shell code that must run in the calling shell:
raw binary: `eval "$(aida role enter advisor)"` via the shell helper (`aida dev shell-init`): just
`aida role enter advisor` The helper auto-evals it, so the bare form is correct there

Usage: aida role enter [OPTIONS] [NAME]

Arguments:
  [NAME]
          Role name — picker shown when omitted on a TTY

Options:
      --cd
          Restore the role's last working directory (cd in the eval output)

      --no-resume
          Skip the interactive recent-session resume prompt

      --no-title
          Do not set the terminal/tab title for this role enter

      --delegate-seat <DELEGATE_SEATS>
          Explicitly allow this session to issue child grants for this seat. May be repeated;
          omitted means this session cannot delegate seats

      --ttl <TTL>
          Grant time-to-live duration (e.g. 72h), capped by [seat] max_grant_hours (default 24, hard
          ceiling 168h)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)

===== aida role expiry
Report how close this session's seat grant is to expiry. By default prints a one-line warning on
stdout when the grant expires within `--warn-within` (or has expired), and nothing otherwise; always
exits 0. With `--refuse-within`, prints the refusal on stderr and exits 3 when less than that is
left: a relay runs it before launching each seat session; it also exits 3 when `AIDA_SESSION_GRANT`
is set but its grant can't be used (missing, malformed, or revoked). No grant at all, or an
implementer grant, is never refused

Usage: aida role expiry [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --warn-within <WARN_WITHIN>
          Warn when the grant expires within this span (e.g. `2h`, `90m`)
          
          [default: 2h]

      --refuse-within <REFUSE_WITHIN>
          Exit 3 with a refusal when less than this span is left

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida session
Inspect or resume past Claude Code sessions in this project, enriched with the AIDA role +
most-recent spec for each session (extracted from the SessionStart hook output stored in each
session's `.jsonl`). Wrapper around `claude --resume` since Claude Code's auto-generated subject
can't be customized

Usage: aida session [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  conversations  List recent Claude Code conversations for this project (cwd) with role + spec
                 context extracted from each conversation's .jsonl. By default shows conversations
                 with activity in the last 24 hours, up to 20 entries — `--all` bypasses the recency
                 cutoff
  resume         Pick a session interactively and resume it via `claude --resume`. When `id` is
                 given, resume that session directly without the picker. The picker shows the same
                 enriched columns as `list`
  focus          Focus the terminal pane/window for a live registered AIDA session
  send           Send text to a live registered AIDA session through its terminal adapter
  new            Launch a new Claude Code session, recording the active role + a user-chosen title
                 so `aida session list` can show them reliably (instead of greping the
                 auto-generated subject). Execs `claude` once the launch metadata is recorded. By
                 default this is a faithful launch — Claude's own native permission posture (it
                 prompts). Turn on bypass for the whole fleet with `[agents] bypass = true` in
                 `~/.aida/agents.toml` (project `.aida/agents.toml` overrides), or per-launch with
                 `--permission-mode`
  start          Start a scoped session: create a sibling git worktree on a fresh branch, symlink
                 AIDA state, and record a lease declaring this session owns a logical or physical
                 scope (an EPIC, SPEC-ID, or path glob). v1 leases are advisory — `aida edit` /
                 `aida-pickup` don't enforce them yet, but multiple sessions running concurrently
                 can use the lease list to coordinate
  end            End a scoped session: remove the worktree, delete the lease, leave the branch alone
                 (merge/discard is up to the user). When `id` is omitted, ends the session whose
                 lease names this cwd's worktree
  leases         List active session leases — the canonical "who holds what scoped work right now"
                 view
  show           Show details for one session lease (defaults to the lease covering cwd, or matched
                 by ancestor PID). Accepts an 8-char id prefix. Output: scope, branch, worktree,
                 inherited role, owner, hostname, lease file path, recent activity entries from the
                 session log, and liveness (live claude in the worktree)
  handoff        Probe whether it is safer to start a fresh agent session or compact the current
                 conversation. This is substrate-only: it can see live drains and this session's
                 live leases, but not conversation-only residue
  seat           Single-occupancy seats: see who drives the orchestrator loop, claim or release it,
                 and hand it over gracefully
  manifest       Manage the planned-cluster manifest for the active session
                 (`.aida/sessions/<id>.manifest.toml`). Used by /aida-pickup to record which items
                 the session intends to work, and by other commands to surface "planned by another
                 session" cues
  prune          Delete Claude Code session metadata (`.jsonl` files under
                 `~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/`) older than N days. Walks the current project + the
                 parent project (when run inside a session worktree). Skips any project dir
                 corresponding to an active `aida session` lease — a defensive guard so the user can
                 run prune from anywhere without clobbering work in progress
  gc             Garbage-collect stale agent isolation worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/agent-*`.
                 CONSERVATIVE by design: a worktree is removed ONLY when ALL of these hold — its
                 branch is merged into the default branch (or it is detached/branchless), the
                 worktree is CLEAN, it is NOT locked, and no live process / active session-lease
                 references it. Anything else is PRESERVED and reported, never removed. Removal uses
                 `git worktree remove` (NOT --force), so git's own safety checks add a second guard;
                 a worktree git refuses to remove is skipped, never forced
  reap           Reap sessions that have genuinely FINISHED — remove the worktree, release the
                 lease, and delete the branch, in one pass, so a headless agent that exited when its
                 work landed doesn't leave a stranded worktree behind for someone to clean up by
                 hand
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida session conversations
List recent Claude Code conversations for this project (cwd) with role + spec context extracted from
each conversation's .jsonl. By default shows conversations with activity in the last 24 hours, up to
20 entries — `--all` bypasses the recency cutoff.

This is the HISTORICAL view (past Claude Code conversations). For the live view of which scoped work
leases are held right now, use `aida session leases`.

The INITIAL TOPIC column is the conversation title Claude Code set at start — it is fixed and does
NOT track current work, so for a long-running conversation it can read stale. Identify a
conversation by its SPEC + AGE, not the topic.

Usage: aida session conversations [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --limit <LIMIT>
          Show at most N conversations (default 20)
          
          [default: 20]

      --no-color
          Plain output (no color), suitable for piping

      --all
          Bypass the default 24h recency cutoff and show every conversation the limit allows

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida session new
Launch a new Claude Code session, recording the active role + a user-chosen title so `aida session
list` can show them reliably (instead of greping the auto-generated subject). Execs `claude` once
the launch metadata is recorded. By default this is a faithful launch — Claude's own native
permission posture (it prompts). Turn on bypass for the whole fleet with `[agents] bypass = true` in
`~/.aida/agents.toml` (project `.aida/agents.toml` overrides), or per-launch with
`--permission-mode`

Usage: aida session new [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -t, --title <TITLE>
          Title for the session (shown in `aida session list`). When omitted, you'll be prompted
          interactively

      --permission-mode <PERMISSION_MODE>
          Claude Code permission mode. When omitted, no `--permission-mode` is injected — Claude
          uses its native posture (the faithful default). Most common explicit values:
          `bypassPermissions` (no prompts), `acceptEdits` (auto-accept edits, prompt other tools),
          `auto` (research preview: auto-approves tool calls with background safety checks),
          `default` (prompt for everything), `plan`. The string is passed straight through to
          `claude --permission-mode`, so any value the installed Claude Code understands works

      --sandbox
          Launch Claude in contained mode: strict Bash sandboxing, no unsandboxed fallback,
          destructive-command deny rules, and project-relative edit auto-allow only

      --role <ROLE>
          Override the role recorded for this session (defaults to $AIDA_SESSION_ROLE)

      --no-title
          Do not set the terminal/tab title for this launch

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida session start
Start a scoped session: create a sibling git worktree on a fresh branch, symlink AIDA state, and
record a lease declaring this session owns a logical or physical scope (an EPIC, SPEC-ID, or path
glob). v1 leases are advisory — `aida edit` / `aida-pickup` don't enforce them yet, but multiple
sessions running concurrently can use the lease list to coordinate

Usage: aida session start [OPTIONS] --owns <SCOPE>

Options:
      --owns <SCOPE>
          Scope this session owns (alias: --spec <SCOPE>). Examples: - `EPIC-N` / `epic-N` (resolved
          against the store) - `FR-N` (any spec id) - `src/scaffolding/**` (path glob — stored, not
          validated) - `feature:auth` (free-form tag)

      --branch <BRANCH>
          Branch name for the new worktree (default: derived from --owns)

      --base <BASE>
          Base branch to fork from (default: current branch)

      --reuse-branch
          Check out the existing `--branch` instead of forking a new one — the
          fixup-on-an-existing-PR-branch flow (e.g. `aida session start --owns PR-N-fixup --branch
          <impl-branch> --reuse-branch`). Errors if the branch exists nowhere. Without this flag, an
          explicitly-named `--branch` that already exists is reused automatically (with a hint), and
          an auto-derived name always forks fresh. `--base` is ignored when reusing

      --path <PATH>
          Worktree directory (default: sibling of project root,
          `<repo-parent>/<repo-name>-<scope-slug>/`)

      --forge <FORGE>
          Forge override for `PR-N` / `MR-N` scopes when the origin URL doesn't auto-detect
          (self-hosted GHE/GitLab, multi-remote setups, etc.). Accepts `github` or `gitlab`

      --branch-style <STYLE>
          Branch naming style when --branch isn't given. `auto` (default): try slug, then
          slug-2..-10, then slug-YYYY-MM-DD, then slug-YYYY-MM-DD-2..-10. `date`:           always
          slug-YYYY-MM-DD (with -N suffix on collision). Useful when every session should be
          traceable to its date
          
          [default: auto]

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -l, --launch
          After creating the worktree + lease, launch Claude Code inside it: chdirs into the
          worktree, records launch metadata in the same log as `aida session new`, then execs
          `claude --permission-mode <mode>`. Collapses the usual "start → cd → session new"
          three-step into one command

  -t, --title <TITLE>
          Title for the launched session (only used with --launch). Shown in `aida session list`.
          Prompted interactively when omitted; pass an empty string to skip the prompt

      --no-title
          Do not set the terminal/tab title for this launch

  -n, --name <NAME>
          Display name passed to Claude Code via `--name`. Shown in claude's prompt box, /resume
          picker, and terminal title. Without this, --launch derives a name from scope+branch+role:
          `review@PR-N` for reviewer sessions, `EPIC-N:batchM` for implementer epic-batch shapes,
          `<role>@<scope>:<suffix>` fallback. Truncated to 64 chars. Only honored with --launch

      --permission-mode <PERMISSION_MODE>
          Claude Code permission mode for the launch. When omitted, no `--permission-mode` is
          injected — Claude uses its native posture (the faithful default; turn on bypass fleet-wide
          with `[agents] bypass = true`). Common explicit values: `bypassPermissions`,
          `acceptEdits`, `auto` (research-preview middle ground — see `aida queue work --help` for
          the tradeoff), `default`, `plan`. Pass-through to `claude --permission-mode`, so any
          installed-claude value works. Ignored without --launch

      --sandbox
          With --launch, launch Claude in contained mode: strict Bash sandboxing, no unsandboxed
          fallback, destructive-command deny rules, and project-relative edit auto-allow only

      --role <ROLE>
          Override the role recorded in this session's lease (and, when `--launch` is set, the
          persona the launched Claude inherits). Without `--role`, the role is derived from the
          scope: `--owns PR-N` / `--owns MR-N` → reviewer; everything else → implementer.
          `$AIDA_SESSION_ROLE` is a last-resort fallback only — when it disagrees with the
          scope-derived default the scope wins and a warning is printed

      --force-claim
          Claim a spec whose status is ambiguous: already In Progress with no local lease (another
          worktree or machine holds it), or NeedsAttention (punted by an autonomous agent and
          awaiting advisor triage). Without this flag those states refuse and ask you to triage
          first. Done / Completed / Rejected / Draft always refuse — `--force-claim` does NOT
          override them

      --pool
          Acquire the session's worktree from the warm-pool (reset a recycled tree instead of
          creating a fresh one — keeps the build cache warm). Overrides the `[worktree_pool]
          enabled` config for this run. Only affects the default new-branch flow (not --reuse-branch
          or PR review checkouts)

      --no-pool
          Force a fresh `git worktree add` even when `[worktree_pool] enabled` is on — the opt-out
          counterpart to `--pool`

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida session end
End a scoped session: remove the worktree, delete the lease, leave the branch alone (merge/discard
is up to the user). When `id` is omitted, ends the session whose lease names this cwd's worktree.

As a side effect, when the just-ended session's branch has an open PR (detected via `gh`), files a
Story-typed review item routed to the `reviewer` role with `implements` relations to every spec
referenced in the PR's commit messages — so a forgotten `gh pr create` doesn't leave the reviewer
unaware.

Usage: aida session end [OPTIONS] [ID]

Arguments:
  [ID]
          Session id (8-char prefix accepted) to end. Omit to end the session matching the current
          cwd. Also accepts a SPEC-ID (e.g. `TASK-<n>` — treated as `--spec`) or a branch name (e.g.
          `task-<n>` — treated as `--branch`) when the lease covering cwd isn't the one you want to
          end

Options:
      --spec <SPEC>
          Resolve the lease by spec ID. Errors when zero or multiple leases own the spec; in the
          multi-match case lists them so you can disambiguate with the lease id

      --branch <BRANCH>
          Resolve the lease by branch name. Errors when zero or multiple leases ride that branch

  -y, --yes
          Skip the y/N confirmation (also implied by `--force`). Required to end a session
          non-interactively — a non-terminal stdin errors without it rather than silently aborting

      --force
          Discard uncommitted work and skip the confirmation. Discards tracked and
          untracked-but-not-ignored changes in the worktree; without this, `session end` refuses and
          prints the dirty file list. Gitignored differences (`target/`, `.aida/cache.db`, etc.)
          never require `--force` and are always discarded. `--force` does NOT override the
          live-process check; that is `--include-in-use`

      --include-in-use
          Remove the worktree, or reset it back into the warm pool, even while live processes use
          it. Without this, `session end` refuses and names each pid and command: a live `claude`
          inside the worktree, or any other process with its working directory, an open or
          memory-mapped file, or its program inside it (a cargo build, for example). With it, live
          `claude` processes inside the worktree are terminated (SIGTERM, 5s grace, then SIGKILL);
          other processes are not killed. Your own shell, its parents and background jobs, and the
          helpers of the agent you are ending from (such as its MCP server) are never counted

      --purge-cc
          After removing the worktree, also delete the corresponding
          `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/` directory so `claude --resume` doesn't try to revive
          sessions whose cwd no longer exists. Without this flag, the dir is left in place and a
          hint is printed pointing at `aida session prune --orphans`

      --wait-ci
          Block until the PR's CI run reaches a terminal state (green or red) before releasing the
          lease — the SILENT variant: polls every 30s and prints only the poll ticks + final result.
          Use it to tail a long/overnight build without prompt noise. For live per-check progress
          instead, use `--watch-ci`. No-op when the session has no associated PR or `gh` isn't on
          PATH

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

      --watch-ci
          Block until CI reaches a terminal state — the LIVE variant: streams `gh run watch` so each
          check resolves on screen as it happens. Use it when you want interactive feedback; use the
          quieter `--wait-ci` to tail a build without the live display. Same end-session decision
          tree as `--wait-ci` once CI is terminal (green proceeds, red prompts)

      --skip-ci
          Skip CI awareness entirely (release the lease without probing the PR's CI run). Use when
          CI is broken, when you're not the one who'll merge, or when the probe would be slow + you
          don't care

      --return
          Return this session's worktree to the warm-pool instead of removing it (now the DEFAULT
          for pooled worktrees): reset it to a clean detached base and mark it idle so the next
          acquire reuses it warm. Kept as an explicit opt-in for back-compat; a pooled tree is
          returned by default unless you pass `--remove`. No-op when the worktree isn't a registered
          pool tree

      --remove
          Delete the worktree instead of returning it to the warm-pool — the opt-out now that
          returning a pooled tree is the default. Forces the old destroy-and-recreate teardown (`git
          worktree remove`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida session leases
List active session leases — the canonical "who holds what scoped work right now" view.

For the historical record of past Claude Code conversations in this project, see `aida session
conversations`.

Usage: aida session leases [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -v, --verbose
          Probe live `claude` processes and warn about ones whose cwd is `(deleted)` — worktree was
          removed without ending claude. `-v` adds two columns: PID of the live claude (when
          present) and the Claude Code session id from `~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/<id>.jsonl`

      --all
          Include stale harness leases in the listing. Every view has a state column (live ● /
          dormant ◐ / stale ⚠). The default view keeps every spec-scoped lease, even a stale one,
          because it still blocks dispatch; it hides only stale harness leases

      --json
          Emit the lease list as JSON for machine consumers. Each lease carries a `drain`
          cross-reference — the orchestrator drain/run driving it (run uuid, phase, mode,
          orchestrator pid), or null when the lease is not the active drain member. Honors `--all`
          (stale leases included) but omits the cross-clone section

      --prune-stale
          Release every CROSS-CLONE lease claim on the shared store that the staleness predicate
          reports dead — past its own `ttl_secs`, or (for a process-backed claim on this host)
          holding a pid whose identity no longer matches. Prints scope + reason per release and
          never touches a claim it reports live, so there is no `--force`. This is the only
          supported way to clear one: `aida session end --spec` cannot reach a foreign claim (it has
          no local lease) and `aida session reap` requires the spec Done + the branch merged + the
          process exited, so the alternative is deleting `.aida-store/coordination/leases/*.toml` by
          hand. Opt-in by design — releasing another clone's claim is a cross-clone mutation, so it
          is never automatic

  -y, --yes
          Skip the y/N confirmation for `--prune-stale`. Required to prune non-interactively — a
          non-terminal stdin errors without it rather than silently releasing another clone's
          claims, the same posture `aida session end` takes

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida session handoff
Probe whether it is safer to start a fresh agent session or compact the current conversation. This
is substrate-only: it can see live drains and this session's live leases, but not conversation-only
residue

Usage: aida session handoff [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --check
          Print the fresh-session vs compact recommendation

      --write <FILE>
          Write a seat handoff note from FILE (`-` reads stdin) under `.aida/handoff/<seat>/` and
          update its `latest.md`. The note is capped at ~4k tokens because it seeds the next session

          fresh session)

      --seat <SEAT>

          `$AIDA_SESSION_ROLE`

      --standing-orders <ACTION> <TEXT>
          Manage the seat's repo-local standing orders (`.aida/standing-orders/<seat>.md`): `add
          "<text>"` appends a dated entry, `list` prints them. `--show` prints standing orders
          before the handoff

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =

===== aida session seat
Single-occupancy seats: see who drives the orchestrator loop, claim or release it, and hand it over
gracefully

Usage: aida session seat [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  claim     Claim an empty seat, or one whose holder has provably exited. Holding it already is
            fine. `--force` asks a live holder to hand it over
  status    Show the holder, its liveness, any pending takeover and in-flight work
  release   Give the seat up. Only the current holder can, at its current generation; with a pending
            takeover, pass its request ID to hand over
  takeover  Ask the live holder to hand the seat over, and wait for its acknowledgment. Nothing is
            stopped if it does not answer in time
  ack       As the holder: confirm you wrote your handoff and stopped dispatching, and hand the seat
            to the pending requester
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

===== aida session seat takeover
Ask the live holder to hand the seat over, and wait for its acknowledgment. Nothing is stopped if it
does not answer in time

Usage: aida session seat takeover [OPTIONS]

      --seat <SEAT>

===== aida session prune
Delete Claude Code session metadata (`.jsonl` files under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/`) older
than N days. Walks the current project + the parent project (when run inside a session worktree).
Skips any project dir corresponding to an active `aida session` lease — a defensive guard so the
user can run prune from anywhere without clobbering work in progress.

Default behavior shows the candidates and asks for confirmation. Use `--dry-run` to preview without
prompting, `--yes` to skip the prompt and delete. Each deletion is appended to
`<project>/.aida/session-prune.log` so the action is auditable.

Usage: aida session prune [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --days <DAYS>
          Delete `.jsonl` files older than N days. Default 30
          
          [default: 30]

      --dry-run
          Show what would be deleted without touching anything. Use to preview before committing to
          a real prune

  -y, --yes
          Skip the y/N confirmation. Without `--dry-run`, deletes immediately after printing the
          candidate list

      --orphans
          Sweep `~/.claude/projects/*` for project dirs whose recorded cwd no longer exists on disk
          (orphans from removed worktrees). When set, each whole orphaned project dir is removed
          instead of file-by-file pruning. Composes with `--dry-run` and `--yes`. `--days` is
          ignored in this mode — orphan-ness is the trigger

      --escalations
          Sweep lingering session worktrees from `--escalate-blocks` punts whose spec has since been
          triaged out of Needs Attention. The autonomous-drain escalation path deliberately leaves
          the worktree alive in case the advisor's resume tier needs it; this flag finds the ones
          that never were resumed and removes the worktree + lease + manifest. Leases whose spec is
          still in Needs Attention are skipped (still awaiting triage). Composes with `--dry-run`
          and `--yes`. `--days` is ignored

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)

          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help

===== aida session gc
Garbage-collect stale agent isolation worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/agent-*`. CONSERVATIVE by
design: a worktree is removed ONLY when ALL of these hold — its branch is merged into the default
branch (or it is detached/branchless), the worktree is CLEAN, it is NOT locked, and no live process
/ active session-lease references it. Anything else is PRESERVED and reported, never removed.
Removal uses `git worktree remove` (NOT --force), so git's own safety checks add a second guard; a
worktree git refuses to remove is skipped, never forced.

Always runs the lossless `git worktree prune` first (clears bookkeeping for already-deleted worktree
dirs). Never runs on the hot `aida status` read path — only on this explicit operator command and on
`aida session end`.

Usage: aida session gc [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --dry-run
          Show what would be removed and what is preserved without touching anything. Use to preview
          before committing to a real GC

  -y, --yes
          Skip the y/N confirmation and remove the eligible worktrees immediately after printing the
          candidate list

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida session reap
Reap sessions that have genuinely FINISHED — remove the worktree, release the lease, and delete the
branch, in one pass, so a headless agent that exited when its work landed doesn't leave a stranded
worktree behind for someone to clean up by hand.

A session is reaped only when ALL of these hold: its spec is Done or Completed, its branch is merged
(an ancestor of the default branch, or a merged PR for the squash case, with zero unique unmerged
commits), and its process has EXITED. Everything else is reported and left exactly as it is.

Reads substrate state only — spec status, branch-merged-ness, process liveness. It never inspects
terminal output to guess whether an agent is finished, and it NEVER closes a running agent: a
session whose process is still alive owns its worktree as its cwd, so it is skipped and reaped on a
later pass once it exits on its own. Dirty worktrees, locked worktrees, and branches carrying unique
unmerged commits are never removed — the same safety checks `aida worktree gc` applies.

A lease held on the main checkout (or another protected checkout) is never reaped, but it is
RELEASED — the lease file only, never a file of the checkout — when the agent process it recorded
(pid plus start identity) is provably dead: gone, or its pid reused by a different process. A lease
that records only the shell that created it, or no pid at all, has an unknown owner and is released
only with --release-unknown-owner. A recorded process that is still running always keeps the lease.

Usage: aida session reap [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --dry-run
          Show what would be reaped and what is left in place without touching anything

  -y, --yes
          Skip the y/N confirmation and reap immediately after printing the candidate list

      --json
          Emit machine-readable JSON

      --release-unknown-owner
          Also release main-checkout leases with an unknown owner (no recorded agent process).
          Without it they are listed and kept

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida lock
Advisor-directed worktree lock — a MANUAL bouncer: `acquire` stamps `authorized_by` on the session
lease covering a worktree, `verify` checks a token against it (exit 0/non-zero, scriptable),
`release` clears it, `status` lists locked worktrees. Additive: nothing today calls `verify`
automatically

Usage: aida lock [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  acquire  Authorize a worktree: stamp `authorized_by = <advisor>` on the session lease covering it.
           Finds the existing lease for the worktree (from `aida session start` / `aida worktree
           enter` / `aida agent new`) and patches it in place; if no lease covers the worktree yet,
           creates a minimal lock-only lease entry so `aida lock verify`/`status` have something to
           read. Re-running re-authorizes (overwrites any prior `authorized_by`)
  verify   Verify a worktree's lock against a token and print the verdict. Exits **0** on `Unlocked`
           or `Authorized`, **non-zero** on `Refused` — scriptable as the manual bouncer (`aida lock
           verify <wt> --as <id> || refuse-to-proceed`)
  release  Clear the `authorized_by` lock on a worktree (no-op if it carries none). Leaves the
           underlying session lease intact; only removes the lock-only entry this command itself
           created when nothing else is on it
  status   List every worktree in this project that currently carries an `authorized_by` lock
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida triage
Acquire / release / inspect a per-scope disposition (triage) lease — the intake gate's "one
disposing advisor per scope" guard. The authority gate decides WHO may dispose; this lease decides
HOW MANY (exactly one live advisor per scope). A second advisor disposing the same scope is refused,
naming the holder. Per-scope, so non- overlapping subsystem advisors dispose concurrently

Usage: aida triage [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  acquire  Take the disposition lease for a scope before disposing drafts in it. Refused (naming the
           holder) if a live advisor already holds the scope. Idempotent for the same process
           re-acquiring. Default scope is the whole project
  release  Release the disposition lease for a scope you hold (no-op if you don't hold it)
  status   Show the live disposition leases for this project (dead-holder leases are reaped on
           read). `--json` for machine consumers
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
