===== aida ship
The one-shot HUMAN-implementer finish. From inside a worktree where you implemented a spec, run the
whole finish ceremony in ONE command: commit any uncommitted work with the (SPEC-ID) trailer, rebase
onto current origin/main, push, open the PR, wait for CI green, squash-merge, run `aida pull` (Done
→ Completed auto-bump), and remove the worktree.

It is the orchestrator's finish phases with phase-1 (implement) done by you instead of a spawned
agent — the human-implementer counterpart to `aida queue work <id> --auto-complete`. The spec is
resolved from the current branch (or the active session lease); pass `<spec>` to override.

Stop earlier with `--no-merge` (open the PR, don't merge) or `--no-pr` (just rebase + push).
`--keep-worktree` leaves the worktree in place after a successful merge.

Usage: aida ship [OPTIONS] [SPEC]

Arguments:
  [SPEC]
          Spec to finish. When omitted, resolved from the current branch name (e.g. `<spec>-ship` →
          `<SPEC-ID>`) or the active session lease covering this worktree

Options:
  -m, --message <MSG>
          Commit subject to use when committing uncommitted work. The `(SPEC-ID)` trailer is
          appended automatically. When omitted, a conventional default is used. Ignored when the
          worktree is clean

      --no-merge
          Stop after opening the PR — do not watch CI or merge. The PR is left open for a human to
          review + merge

      --no-pr
          Stop after rebase + push — do not open a PR. Useful when you want to open the PR yourself,
          or when CI is configured to gate on push

      --keep-worktree
          Keep the worktree after a successful merge (skip the `aida session end` cleanup step)

      --dry-run
          Print the resolved finish sequence without executing any of it

      --no-trailer-check
          Bypass the client-side trailer spec-ID check before shipping

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida pr
Pull-request side-effects intended to fire from the /aida-pr skill. Today: `auto-queue-review` files
the reviewer story right after `gh pr create` so the trigger lives where context is freshest. `aida
session end` keeps the same logic as an idempotent backup for PRs opened outside the skill

File the reviewer story for the change (PR/MR) open on the current branch and queue it to the

`aida session end` also fires this as a backup, so a forgotten /aida-pr (or a raw `gh pr create` /
`glab mr create`) still ends up routed to the reviewer. The idempotency guard means both firing is
fine.

===== aida pr rebase
Rebase a PR onto its base in a temporary worktree, then force-push-with-lease the rebased branch.
Collapses the standard 6-command "rebase a PR before review" recipe into one call.

Default mode aborts cleanly on conflicts (cleans up the temp worktree, prints the manual recipe,
exits non-zero). `--check` reports stale-base + overlap + conflict-prediction without modifying
anything. `--interactive` drops into the temp worktree on conflict so you can resolve + continue,
then AIDA finishes the push. Cross-fork PRs are refused (force-push to a fork is the contributor's
job).

Force-push always uses `--force-with-lease`. The smoke check (default `cargo build --release` for
Rust projects) is configurable via `.aida/config.toml` `[pr-rebase] smoke_check`.

Usage: aida pr rebase [OPTIONS] <N>

Arguments:
  <N>
          PR number to rebase

Options:
      --check
          Report-only: don't modify anything. Prints stale-base, overlapping files, and a
          best-effort conflict prediction

      --interactive
          On conflict, leave the temp worktree in place and prompt you to resolve + `git rebase
          --continue`, then finish the push

      --no-smoke
          Skip the post-rebase build smoke check

      --base <REF>
          Rebase onto this explicit base ref instead of the PR's declared base. Useful for PRs
          against non-main branches

      --onto-parent <SHA>
          Stack-aware rebase: replay only the commits AFTER this SHA (the recorded fork-point of the
          branch this PR was stacked on), via `git rebase --onto <base> <SHA>`. Use when the stacked
          parent was squash-merged and its branch deleted — a plain rebase would re-apply the
          parent's pre-squash commits. Refused when SHA is not an ancestor of the PR head (a stale
          stack record)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida pr ship
Ship a PR: create-if-needed → watch CI → squash-merge → pull → worktree-aware cleanup. The
direct-publish counterpart to `aida queue work PR-N --auto-complete` (which drives the full reviewer
pipeline) — use this for human-pre-approved work where no orchestrator review phase is needed (docs
PRs, master-signed architecture work, recovery merges).

With no `<N>`, the command targets the current branch's open PR — creating one via `gh pr create`
(deriving title/body from the latest commit) if none exists. `aida pull` runs from the main worktree
even when invoked from a sibling worktree, and the merge step detects branches checked out in
sibling worktrees before deciding whether `--delete-branch` is safe — both papercuts surfaced by the
2026-05-22 stopgap-shell experience.

Composes with the transient-retry layer for the `gh` calls (sub-second network blips no longer abort
the flow).

Usage: aida pr ship [OPTIONS] [N]

Arguments:
  [N]
          PR number to ship. When omitted, the command resolves the PR open on the current branch
          (or creates one if none exists)

Options:
      --no-pull
          Skip the post-merge `aida pull`. Useful when shipping from inside a composition that pulls
          separately

      --no-cleanup
          Skip the `aida session end` worktree-cleanup step. Useful when you want to inspect the
          post-merge state before the worktree disappears

      --dry-run
          Print the resolved sequence without executing any of it

      --wait [<SECS>]
          Bound drive ownership plus CI registration/settlement wait in seconds. Bare --wait uses
          300 seconds; omitted leaves CI unbounded and refuses drive-owned PRs immediately. Drive
          seats always refuse immediately. Exit codes: 20 CI red, 21 CI timeout, 22 not mergeable,
          23 review, 24 stale CI definition, 25 merge hold (0 merged/already merged)

      --force-delete-branch
          Delete the merged branch even when branches/PRs are stacked on it. Without this, ship
          keeps the branch alive when it detects stacked children, so deleting it can't auto-close
          their PRs; pass this to orphan the children deliberately

      --complexity <LEVEL>
          Implementer's self-assessed actual complexity at ship time: `low` / `med` / `high`.
          Captured to `.aida/complexity-calibration/<SPEC>.yaml` alongside the punt count from
          `.aida/punts.jsonl` — feeds the three-way calibration view (`aida autonomy calibration
          mismatches`). Best-effort, not graded: estimate is a substrate-knowledge signal, never an
          approval criterion. Absent ⇒ ship slot records only the punt count
          
          [possible values: low, med, high]

      --effort <BUCKET>
          Implementer's actual effort spent: 15m, 1h, 4h, 1d, or 1w. Captured to
          `.aida/effort-calibration/<SPEC>.yaml` as the ship/implementation touchpoint. `1d` is 8
          work-hours; `1w` is 40 work-hours
          
          [possible values: 15m, 1h, 4h, 1d, 1w]

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

      --no-trailer-check
          Bypass the client-side trailer spec-ID check (Guard 1). Ship even when a commit's
          `(SPEC-ID)` trailer does not resolve to a live spec. Use only when you know the trailer is
          intentional (e.g. a cross-repo id the local store can't see)

      --override-stale-check
          Ship even when the PR's green check completed before a CI-definition file (a workflow, or
          a script it invokes directly) changed on the base branch. Without this, ship refuses so a
          green that no longer means what it looks like doesn't merge unnoticed. A plain test-file
          change on the base branch only warns and never needs this flag

      --override-stale-approval
          Ship even when the PR's newest recorded approval does not cover its current head — the
          head moved past the approved commit, the approval names no commit, or the head could not
          be read. Without this, ship refuses: re-review the current head instead

      --no-complete
          Ship this PR as a non-completing slice: write no completing `(SPEC-ID)` trailer into the
          squash subject from any source (title trailer or branch name), so the merge completes no
          spec. Use for one PR of a multi-PR spec. A PR body line reading `aida: no-complete` or
          `Non-completing slice` has the same effect; and the branch-name fallback is skipped on its
          own when the spec carries `closure:pending` or has open slice children

      --rebase
          Rebase-merge the PR (`gh pr merge --rebase --match-head-commit <SHA>`) instead of
          squash-merging, preserving each slice commit on the base branch. Runs the same approval,
          authority, CI, and merge-hold gates as squash. Rebase merges produce no squash subject and
          complete no spec unless `--final-slice` is also passed

      --merge-method <METHOD>
          Explicit merge method (`squash` or `rebase`). Equivalent to `--rebase` when set to
          `rebase`
          
          [possible values: squash, rebase]

      --final-slice
          Complete the PR's resolved spec(s) after a `--rebase` merge lands. Without this flag, a
          rebase merge treats the PR as a non-completing slice and leaves the owning spec's status
          unchanged
          
          [aliases: --complete-spec]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Exit codes: 0 merged (or already merged; dry-run previews); 1 other error; 20 CI red; 21
ownership/CI wait timed out; 22 needs rebase/not mergeable; 23 needs review/approval at head; 24
stale CI definition; 25 merge-hold present.
===== aida pr ship-batch
Ship several PRs that need a human merge, one at a time, in order.

For each PR, in the order given, it refreshes the branch from main only when the PR is behind or its
green predates a CI-definition change, waits for CI on that exact head, waits for an independent
approval recorded at that head (it queues the PR for review but never records a verdict), then asks
you to type the PR number before shipping it with every `aida pr ship` gate in force. A merge-hold
on a confirmed PR is cleared only when you also type `clear`.

Any failure stops the batch without shipping: red or missing CI, a conflict, no approval in time, a
refused gate, or an unconfirmed prompt. Re-run the same command to continue; merged PRs are skipped.
Runs only for a human at an interactive terminal, on GitHub.

Usage: aida pr ship-batch [OPTIONS] <PR>...

Arguments:
  <PR>...
          PR numbers, shipped in exactly this order (at most 20, no repeats)

Options:
      --review-timeout <DURATION>
          How long to wait for an approval at each PR's head, e.g. `45m`, `2h` (a bare number is
          minutes; default 60m)

      --dry-run
          Show each PR's state and what the batch would do; change nothing. It does not fetch:
          staleness is judged against your local `origin/*` refs as they are

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida pr hold
Deliberately HOLD the PR on the current session — push the branch but intentionally do not open the
PR yet, pending a manual gate (a smoke test, an out-of-band review, an operator decision).

Under an `--auto-complete` drain this is a clean finish outcome, NOT a failure: the orchestrator
reads the hold signal this writes and reports a `Held` outcome (branch pushed, PR held) with the
right recovery hint instead of mis-filing the missing PR as a phase-1 failure. Resolve the spec +
branch from the active session lease; record `{spec, branch, reason}` for the orchestrator
handshake.

Usage: aida pr hold [OPTIONS]

===== aida pr gc
Sweep local review-snapshot branches (`pr-N` / `mr-N`, created by `aida session start --owns PR-N` /
`aida pr rebase` when they fetch a change's head ref for headless review) whose change has reached a
terminal state (merged or closed). Nothing removes these today, so a long-running project's local
branch namespace accumulates one per review, forever.

A candidate is deleted only when: the change is merged/closed (an open change is left alone — the
review may still need it), the branch isn't checked out in any worktree, and the branch's tip still
matches the change's last known head SHA (a branch that gained local commits since the fetch is left
alone rather than guessed at). Every skip is reported with its reason. Scoped to the exact
`pr-<digits>` / `mr-<digits>` name shape `aida session start --owns PR-N` creates — never touches an
authored spec branch.

Opt-in: this command is never run automatically. Use `--dry-run` to preview before deleting.

Usage: aida pr gc [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --dry-run
          Report what would be deleted without deleting anything

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida zen
One-shot AUTONOMOUS implement + ship from a spec OR a one-line thought. Pass an approved spec id to
drive it; pass free text to draft a spec from the thought, file it, and drive that — thought to
(gated) merged in one line. Auto-queues the spec, then drives it through the SAME `--auto-complete`
orchestrator `aida burndown` uses (implement → CI → review → merge → pull). FULLY HEADLESS by
default — kick one off and walk away; an INDEPENDENT reviewer always runs before the auto-merge.
Drives are SERIALIZED per repo: a global drain lock allows one drive at a time, so a second `aida
zen` while one is live is refused. To drive several specs at once, use the `aida burndown` fan-out —
one orchestrator over worktree-isolated implementer subagents. Use `--supervised` to drive the
implementer yourself. The auto-implement counterpart to `aida ship` (which finishes a
HUMAN-implemented spec). With no argument, prints help

Usage: aida zen [OPTIONS] [SPEC]

Arguments:
  [SPEC]
          An approved SPEC id to drive, OR a free-text thought to draft into a spec and drive. Free
          text is drafted into a title + description + acceptance criteria, filed as a draft, then
          routed through the approve-gate before driving

Options:
      --supervised
          Supervised drive: YOU drive the implementer interactively, and the reviewer still runs
          headless as an independent gate before the auto-merge. The opt-in counterpart to the
          fire-and-forget default (which runs the implementer headless too). Maps to the
          orchestrator's `--no-human=reviewer-only`

      --no-human [<MODE>]
          Explicit autonomy mode override, forwarded to the orchestrator. The reviewer ALWAYS runs
          headless as an independent gate; this only governs the implementer. The DEFAULT is `both`
          (fully headless fire-and-forget — kick one off and walk away; drives are serialized per
          repo, use `aida burndown` to drive several specs at once). `--no-human=reviewer-only` (=
          `--supervised`) keeps the implementer interactive. Aliases: `--unattended`, `--headless`

      --no-pull
          Skip the post-merge `aida pull` (the Done → Completed auto-bump) — forwarded to the
          orchestrator

      --force
          Override the soft suitability warnings (under-specified / coupled) and drive anyway. Does
          NOT override the hard refusals (epic, keystone, blocked)

      --solo
          Own worktree + own PR: split this spec out of its scope (parent epic / active focus)
          instead of routing into the scope worktree. The explicit exception to the
          default-into-scope routing

      --into-epic
          Force the cluster route: drive inside the scope (parent epic / focus) worktree even when
          the default would otherwise pick its own. The counterpart to `--solo`

      --dry-run
          Resolve + validate the spec and PRINT the plan WITHOUT driving it

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

      --json
          Emit the drive-suitability GATE VERDICT as JSON and exit WITHOUT driving — the
          machine-readable pre-flight a shell-out consumer (the TUI drive verb) reads to surface a
          gate hold, and its clarify / force remedy, instead of a false "drive launched". Implies a
          dry run; needs a real SPEC id (not a free-text thought)

      --vendor <VENDOR>
          Which vendor CLI runs the headless implementer for this drive: `claude`, `codex`, or `agy`
          (alias: `--agent`, matching `aida agent new <vendor>`). A per-invocation override — no
          need to export `AIDA_HEADLESS_VENDOR` just to drive one spec on Codex. Resolution order:
          this flag > the `AIDA_HEADLESS_VENDOR` env > the `[orchestrator] headless_vendor` /
          `[agents] vendor` config knob > `claude` (default)
          
          [aliases: --agent]

      --compete
          2-agent bake-off: fan claude + codex to INDEPENDENTLY implement this spec in separate
          worktrees (same acceptance, no shared context), run each candidate's CI (a failing
          candidate is eliminated), have ONE BLIND reviewer score the passers side-by-side (vendor
          identity stripped), merge the winner into the current branch, delete the loser branch, and
          record the outcome (a CompeteOutcome row in `.aida/events.jsonl` + a spec comment) for
          dispatch-policy data. Premium mode — 2x implement cost; best for hard/ambiguous specs

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida zen needs-human
Mark the current `--zen` session as having needed a human — call it the moment the session pauses on
a design-fork for the standby advisor or raises a punt. Its presence makes `aida zen finish` pause
at the grab-next/stop checkpoint rather than auto-exiting

Usage: aida zen needs-human [OPTIONS] --reason <TEXT>

Options:

===== aida drain
Inspect the active `aida queue work --auto-complete` drain — what command launched it, the batch
members and their progress, and what happens to the queue when the current session exits. If a spec
will not drain because it needs guided/operator attention, de-risk it with `aida derisk <ID>`

Usage: aida drain [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  start   Start an autonomous drain through the canonical `queue work --auto-complete` engine
  resume  Re-drive a deliberately shelved spec from the phase that failed
  stop    Request that the live drain stop at the next spec boundary
  status  Show the active drain: the launching command, the members and their lifecycle state, the
          current phase, and a prediction of what happens on session exit. Launcher-held drains
          (`aida burndown run`, `aida queue integrate`) are reported from the live drain lock — pid,
          start time, and spec set — even though they write no per-phase progress file. Prints `No
          drain in progress.` (exit 0) when none is running. A drain-state file whose orchestrator
          process is no longer alive is reported as stale — `--clear` removes it
  clear   Remove a stale drain-state file
  tail    Stream the active drain log, using the same resolver and renderer as `aida tail drain`
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida drain start
Start an autonomous drain through the canonical `queue work --auto-complete` engine

Usage: aida drain start [OPTIONS] [SELECTOR]

Arguments:
  [SELECTOR]
          Optional selector: a SPEC id, `next`, `nextN`, or `batch:NAME`

Options:
      --project <PATH>
          Resolve and run against this project instead of the current cwd

      --batch <NAME>
          Drain a named `batch:NAME`

      --once
          Drive exactly the queue head (`aida queue work next --auto-complete`)

      --no-human [<MODE>]
          Headless mode for the canonical drain. Bare flag means `both`

      --role <NAME>
          Override the drain role

      --max-failures <N>
          Per-batch failure budget passed through to the engine

      --max-iterations <N>
          Stop after this many acted-on specs

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

      --max-runtime <DUR>
          Stop after this wall-clock budget (`90s`, `45m`, `2h`)

      --max-tokens <N>
          Cap cumulative reported tokens

      --json
          Emit JSON progress from the underlying drain

      --vendor <VENDOR>
          Route the headless agents to a vendor (`claude`, `codex`, `agy`)
          
          [aliases: --agent]

      --model <MODEL>
          Opaque model override passed through to the selected vendor

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida stack
Inspect the stacked-branch graph: `aida queue work --stack` records each stacked branch's parent in
`.aida/stacks.json`; `aida stack show` / `list` render the chains. Pairs with the auto-rebase
cascade that `aida pull --auto` runs when a base merges

Usage: aida stack [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  show  Render the stack tree — one indented line per branch, grouped by chain. Stale entries
        (branch missing locally + on origin) are suffixed with `(stale)` and can be cleaned by
        passing `--prune-stale`
  list  One line per chain in the form `bottom → mid → top`. Quieter than `show`; useful for scripts
        and the statusline
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

clean text instead of pages of `null`

        the most-recently- modified log under `.aida/headless-logs/`; pass a SPEC-ID to pick the
        newest log for that spec, or a lease/session id prefix (e.g. `019e4400`) to disambiguate
        between concurrent drains
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

===== aida headless tail
Stream a headless-drain JSONL log as clean text — one block of assistant prose per message, blank
line between messages. No daemon, no parsing into cache.db. With no argument, picks the
most-recently- modified log under `.aida/headless-logs/`; pass a SPEC-ID to pick the newest log for
that spec, or a lease/session id prefix (e.g. `019e4400`) to disambiguate between concurrent drains

Usage: aida headless tail [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]
          SPEC-ID (e.g. `TASK-N`) or lease/session id prefix. Optional — when omitted, the
          most-recently-modified log is followed

Options:
      --list
          List every log file under `.aida/headless-logs/` (kind, spec, mtime, size, filename) and
          exit. Useful for picking a lease id when multiple drains have touched the same spec

      --with-tools
          Interleave tool invocations as `[ToolName] <preview>` lines, alongside the assistant text.
          Off by default — most users only want the narration

      --tools-only
          Print only tool invocations, no assistant text. Useful for watching what commands the
          implementer is running

      --include-user
          Also surface `type=="user"` messages (tool_result payloads). Off by default — headless
          mode rarely has interactive user content, and tool_results add a lot of noise

  -n, --no-follow
          Print existing content and exit instead of staying attached with `tail -f`-style polling.
          Useful for piping into a pager

      --since <DURATION>
          Skip entries older than this point: a relative duration (`30s`, `10m`, `2h`, `1d`, `2w`,
          or `24 hours ago`; a bare integer means seconds), an ISO date (`2026-05-01`, local
          midnight), a zone-less ISO datetime (local time), or RFC3339. Compared against `timestamp`
          fields when the event carries one; events without a timestamp (assistant messages, system
          events) pass through unfiltered

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida worker

Usage: aida worker [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

              `aida-worker` shell function will act on is at the top. Prints `No pending
              directives.` (exit 0) when the file is empty or absent
  gc          Garbage-collect stale directives from `.aida/worker.cmd` — prune every spec-targeted
              drain line whose target spec is already archived, Completed, or Rejected, so a later
              worker run cannot fire an unattended drain against finished work. Bare drains,
              batch-scoped drains, comments, and control directives (pause / exit) are never
              touched. Sibling of `aida queue gc` (which prunes dead routed queue entries)
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

===== aida brief

          Agent name for brief creation, e.g. codex or antigravity

Options:

          SPEC-ID this brief must be picked up after

      --as-deep-link
          Print a `claude-cli://open` deep link after writing the brief. Click → Claude Code opens
          in the spec's worktree with a short pickup prompt (inert until Enter). Eliminates the
          paste step. Requires Claude Code v2.1.91+ for the URL scheme

      --notify
          Mark the brief urgent: write a `.pending` sentinel so an idle agent's `aida status` (and
          statusline) surfaces it without a heartbeat. Omit for FYI-only briefs that shouldn't
          interrupt

      --authorized-by <AUTHORIZED_BY>
          The advisor id authorizing this brief's target worktree. Recorded on the brief and, if the
          receiving agent is launched with `aida agent new ... --spec <SPEC>` after this brief
          exists, carried into that session's role-context snapshot — the token the automatic
          advisor-lock gate reads at commit time under `[locking] posture = "warn"`/`"enforce"`

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

===== aida compete
Run one spec through N vendors headless, in isolated worktrees, then an objective gate — the neutral
cross-vendor quality layer. For each vendor AIDA creates a per-vendor worktree+branch, assembles the
implementer brief from the spec, runs the vendor headless (claude/codex), commits the result, and
runs a deterministic gate that mirrors PR CI by default (fmt-check + build + tests + clippy +
glyph-lint, so a gate-passing winner is actually mergeable). Reports a table, ranks the gate-passers
(smaller/focused diff first), optionally runs a rubric LLM judge (--judge), and leaves every branch
in place to pick. Report-only: it recommends a winner but never merges

Usage: aida compete [OPTIONS] <SPEC>

Arguments:
  <SPEC>
          SPEC-ID (or UUID) to run through the vendors

Options:
      --vendors <VENDORS>
          Comma-separated vendors to run, e.g. `claude,codex`. Headless vendors run directly; a
          non-headless vendor (antigravity) is emitted as a human-run brief instead

      --gate <GATE>
          Override the deterministic gate command run in each worktree. Default mirrors PR CI:
          fmt-check + build + the aida-cli test suite + clippy correctness + glyph-lint, so a
          gate-passing winner is mergeable. Pass your own command for non-Rust repos / custom CI

      --dry-run
          Assemble the briefs + plan the run and print what WOULD happen without spawning any vendor
          or touching git

      --judge
          Add a rubric LLM judge after the gate: spawn a `claude -p` judge over the spec + each
          candidate's diff, scoring spec-adherence / correctness / simplicity / test-coverage (1-5)
          and recommending a winner. Opt-in and REPORT-ONLY — it never merges; the human/advisor
          still picks. The cheap deterministic ranking (smaller, focused diff first) is always shown
          regardless of this flag

      --judge-vendor <JUDGE_VENDOR>
          Which vendor renders the rubric judgment (claude or codex). The judge PROMPT is identical
          for both — only the executing model changes — so a codex judge over a claude-vs-codex run
          is no longer the same model grading itself, removing the self-evaluation caveat. Defaults
          to claude (unchanged behaviour). Set AIDA_COMPETE_JUDGE to override the judge binary. Only
          applies with --judge
          
          [default: claude]

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured

===== aida agent

Usage: aida agent [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:

  stop             Stop an active agent process by name

  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

===== aida agent new
Launch a new agent process.

This lane spawns an INTERACTIVE agent in the foreground and BLOCKS until that agent's session exits.
A vendor TUI does not exit when its turn ends — it returns to its prompt — so a seat that has
finished its work still holds this command. Budget for that: run it where you can leave it, or stop
the seat with `aida agent stop <name>` once it reports. To tell a finished seat from a working one
without attaching, read the CPU column in `aida agent status`: seconds of CPU across hours of age
means the seat is idle at its prompt. Do NOT rely on the `status` column for that — it reports
`busy` for a seat whose worktree any live lease covers, which for the main checkout is effectively
always.

It is also NOT the orchestrated pipeline — it does not run CI, the reviewer phase, or the merge for
you. For a supervised end-to-end drain (implementer → CI → reviewer → merge → pull), use `aida queue
work <SPEC> --auto-complete` instead.

Usage: aida agent new [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  claude       Spawn Claude Code with project-correct cwd/env and registry tracking
  codex        Spawn Codex CLI with project-correct cwd/env and registry tracking
  antigravity  Spawn Antigravity CLI with project-correct cwd/env and registry tracking
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida agent new claude
Spawn Claude Code with project-correct cwd/env and registry tracking

Usage: aida agent new claude [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --role <ROLE>
          Role propagated to the spawned Claude process as AIDA_SESSION_ROLE

      --spec <SPEC>
          SPEC-ID to work. Creates a scoped worktree + lease before launch

      --force
          Override the focus-scope drift guard: launch on a spec outside the active `aida focus`
          subtree even when `[focus] out_of_scope = "block"` would refuse, and silence the `warn`
          nudge

      --cwd <PATH>
          AIDA project root or descendant used as the launch base

      --permission-mode <PERMISSION_MODE>
          Claude Code permission mode passed through to `claude`. When omitted, no
          `--permission-mode` is injected — Claude uses its native posture (the faithful default;
          turn on bypass fleet-wide with `[agents] bypass = true` in agents.toml)

      --model <MODEL>
          Opaque Claude model name passed through as `claude --model`. Overrides `[agents.claude]
          model`; AIDA does not validate it

      --sandbox
          Launch Claude in contained mode: strict Bash sandboxing, no unsandboxed fallback,
          destructive-command deny rules, and project-relative edit auto-allow only

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

      --no-context
          Do not write/inject the AIDA launch-context snapshot

      --no-title
          Do not set the terminal/tab title for this launch

      --show-context
          Print the generated launch-context snapshot before spawning

      --no-exec
          Print the complete resolved launch contract — argv, active role, prompt source,
          launch-context snapshot path, AIDA environment inputs, and repository guidance files
          (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) the child would consume — then exit without spawning a process,
          creating a worktree/lease, flipping spec status, or any network sync. See also
          `--show-prompt` (just the initial prompt) and `--show-context` (the full launch-context
          markdown body)
          
          [aliases: --noexec, --print-command]

      --show-prompt
          Print the exact initial prompt (explicit `--prompt` or the auto-generated one) that would
          be sent, then exit without spawning or any other side effect

      --verbose
          For a launch that actually executes: print launch-time diagnostics (resolved
          vendor/client, role, spec/session/name, working directory, prompt source and whether
          context was injected, guidance files discovered, generated child argv with sensitive
          values redacted, process registration, and child exit/result information) before/around
          spawn. Distinct from `--no-exec`, which previews and exits without launching; `--verbose`
          launches. Never prints secrets, tokens, full prompt contents, or sensitive environment
          values. Normal (non-verbose) output is unchanged

      --prompt <PROMPT>
          Initial message to pass to the spawned Claude session

      --prompt-file <PATH>
          Read the initial message from a file instead of the command line. Prefer this from
          orchestrators: a brief passed as `--prompt "$(cat file)"` through a nested shell can lose
          its quoting and silently launch an agent that sits idle at an empty prompt

      --no-prompt
          Do not send the automatic role-aware initial message

      --no-resume
          Skip the ended-session resume offer

      --resume <latest|NAME>
          Resume the latest ended matching session, or a named ended session, without prompting

      --allow-duplicate
          Skip the live-duplicate confirmation prompt while still checking for duplicates

      --no-duplicate-check
          Skip the live same-vendor/same-role duplicate check entirely

      --no-default-flags
          Do not read per-agent default flags from ~/.aida/agents.toml or .aida/agents.toml

      --extra-flag <FLAG>
          Append one additional raw flag to the spawned Claude argv

      --name <NAME>
          Optional human-readable instance name

      --description <DESCRIPTION>
          Optional human-readable description of this agent session

      --bg
          Dispatch to Claude Code's background supervisor via `claude --bg`. The session detaches
          from this terminal and shows up in `claude agents` (and `aida status`). When `--spec` is
          also passed, AIDA records the captured sessionId on the lease so the cross-substrate view
          links them automatically. Without `--bg`, the foreground launch path is unchanged. For
          non-interactive dispatch, first set `[agents] confirm_bypass = false` in
          `~/.aida/config.toml`; trusted project config can still require consent. Then use: `aida
          agent new claude --bg --role implementer --spec <ID> --cwd <WORKTREE> --prompt-file <FILE>
          --no-resume --permission-mode bypassPermissions`. An explicit owning cwd reuses its
          inactive same-role lease; it never takes over a live agent

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida state-snapshot
Emit the seven-row finish-state preamble (Spec / Branch / PR / Drain / Tests / Fmt / Plan)
deterministically. One source of truth for every `/aida-pickup` and `/aida-pr` next-steps template —
the rows used to be filled in by hand from `git status`, `gh pr view`, `aida show`, `aida session
show`, and drifted between sibling skills. Hidden: skill-internal, not a daily-driver command

Usage: aida state-snapshot [OPTIONS] --spec <SPEC>

Options:
      --spec <SPEC>
          SPEC-ID whose title + status appear on the Spec row

      --tests <TESTS>
          Free-form summary of the last `cargo test` run, used as the Tests row. Default `"not run"`
          — the caller (skill) is the authoritative source for transient runtime state
          
          [default: "not run"]

      --fmt <FMT>
          Free-form summary of the last `cargo fmt --check`, used as the Fmt row. Default `"not
          run"` — same rationale as `--tests`
          
          [default: "not run"]

      --json
          Emit the snapshot as JSON instead of the fixed-width text block. For Step 5b finding
          metadata (machine-readable snapshot beside the finding's prose body)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida statusbar
Ambient terminal-title meter — a read-only project pulse riding the
terminal title bar (any OSC-capable terminal; tmux shows it as the
window title). On an interval, emits the set-window-title escape with
a compact meter: queue depth, live/STALE session counts, and how many
items await you (briefs · findings · mail · punts). Purely an ambient
signal — it dispatches nothing, launches nothing, writes nothing; all
sources are cache/local-fast (no network, PRs omitted).

Examples:
  aida statusbar                 # refresh the title every 15s (Ctrl+C exits)
  aida statusbar --restore-title # same, restoring the previous title on exit
  aida statusbar --once          # single title update (shell prompt hooks)
  aida statusbar --plain         # print the meter as plain text and exit

tmux status-right recipe (plain text, no escapes needed):
  set -g status-right '#(aida statusbar --plain) '
  set -g status-interval 15

Usage: aida statusbar [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --interval <INTERVAL>
          Seconds between title refreshes in loop mode (minimum 2)
          
          [default: 15]

      --once
          Emit ONE title update and exit — for wiring into a shell PROMPT_COMMAND / precmd hook
          instead of running the loop

      --plain
          Print the meter as a plain text line (no escape sequence) and exit — the building block
          for tmux's status-right interpolation

      --restore-title
          Save the current terminal title on start and restore it when the loop exits (XTerm
          title-stack escapes). Opt-in: not every terminal implements the title stack

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida statusline
One-line project + role summary suitable for shell prompts and the `statusLine.command` setting in
~/.claude/settings.json. Sub-50ms (reads the cache + the orphan-store queue YAML). Format: aida ·
<project> · role:<name> · @SPEC · q:N · cache:fresh|stale Where `q:N` is the depth of the queue
routed to the active role (omitted when zero)

Usage: aida statusline [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  title  Emit the one-liner as an OSC terminal-title escape sequence
  setup  Print (or install) client-appropriate statusline configuration so a user can enable the
         AIDA-aware statusline segment. Prints by default; pass `--install` to write the supported
         client's `settings.json` entry
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --color <COLOR>
          When to emit ANSI color: `auto` (default — color iff stdout is a TTY and `NO_COLOR` is
          unset), `always`, `never`
          
          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, always, never]

      --client <CLIENT>
          Merge live fields from a client's stdin JSON payload into the AIDA segment: model,
          context-window usage, activity, and VCS branch where the client sends them. `claude`
          parses Claude Code's statusLine JSON; `antigravity` (alias `agy`) parses Antigravity's
          live agent-state JSON. Omit for the default, AIDA-only segment — this never reads stdin
          unless a client is named, so plain `aida statusline` is unaffected. When stdin is a TTY
          (no payload piped), or a piped read doesn't finish within ~200ms (an open pipe with no
          data waiting), this degrades to the AIDA-only segment rather than blocking. See
          docs/agents/statusline-contract.md
          
          [possible values: claude, antigravity, agy]

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida statusline setup
Print (or install) client-appropriate statusline configuration so a user can enable the AIDA-aware
statusline segment. Prints by default; pass `--install` to write the supported client's
`settings.json` entry

Usage: aida statusline setup [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --client <CLIENT>
          Which client to emit setup for: `claude` (command-backed statusLine in settings.json),
          `codex` (built-in TUI footer fields — Codex does not run arbitrary commands in its
          footer), `antigravity` (command-backed statusLine plus title command), or `all` (default —
          print guidance for every supported client)
          
          [default: all]
          [possible values: claude, codex, antigravity, all]

      --install
          Install the configuration instead of only printing it. Only the `claude` and `antigravity`
          clients support install (they write/merge the `statusLine` block into settings.json);
          Codex stays print-only because its footer config is hand-edited

      --settings-path <SETTINGS_PATH>
          Antigravity settings path. Defaults to `$AIDA_ANTIGRAVITY_SETTINGS`, then
          `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`

      --replace-default
          For Antigravity, replace its default status line instead of stacking AIDA with it
          (`stack_with_default: false`)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida away
Mark yourself away from the keyboard. Sets a machine-global presence state (a timestamped
`~/.aida/presence.toml` file — no daemon) that stays `away` until its TTL lapses (default 8h) or you
return. An interactive command auto-flips you back to `home`.

Presence is ADVISORY input to mode selection: while away, an `aida queue work --auto-complete` with
no explicit `--no-human` / `--escalate-*` flag defaults to a headless drain; explicit flags always
win and integrity gates (the kickoff scope-ack, CI, merge-on-green) always apply. Tune under
`[presence]` in `.aida/config.toml`: consumers  = "on" | "off"            (master switch; default
on) away_drain = "headless-both"         (default) | "headless-escalate-defaults" | "headless-park"
escalation = "defaults" | "park"     (punt handling; unset = derive from away_drain) home_offer =
"surface" | "dont-block" (home-side; default surface)

Hidden alias for `aida presence away` (kept for muscle memory).

Usage: aida away [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida presence
Operator presence — the home/away state the autonomy ladder keys on. `aida presence` (or `aida
presence status`) shows the current state; `aida presence away` / `aida presence home` set it. While
away, an `aida queue work --auto-complete` with no explicit mode flag defaults to a headless drain
(advisory; integrity gates always apply)

Usage: aida presence [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  away    Mark yourself away from the keyboard (sets the machine-global presence state with a TTL).
          Same as the hidden top-level `aida away`
  home    Mark yourself back at the keyboard (clears any away state). Same as the hidden top-level
          `aida home`
  status  Show current effective presence: home/away, how long ago it was set, and TTL-remaining
          when away. Same as bare `aida presence`
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida solo
Enter solo mode — mark this session as the advisor+integrator working the SAFE backlog end-to-end
with maximum discretion (groom → implement → integrate → repeat), parking keystone/architecture for
you. A timestamped flag (~/.aida/solo.toml, 24h safety TTL) the statusline surfaces. `--off` exits;
`--status` prints current state; `--ttl <DURATION>` overrides the 24h cap (e.g. 8h, 2h30m)

Usage: aida solo [OPTIONS] [ACTION]

Arguments:
  [ACTION]
          What to do: `run` (start the loop), `stop` (stop it), or `status`. Omit to enter solo MODE
          (the work-state flag). The legacy `--watch`/`--off`/`--status` flags are silent aliases
          for run/stop/status

          Possible values:
          - run:    Start the solo loop in the foreground (== legacy `--watch`)
          - stop:   Stop a running solo loop (== legacy `--off`)
          - status: Print whether a solo loop / solo mode is active (== legacy `--status`)

Options:
      --off
          Exit solo mode

      --status
          Print whether solo mode is active, without changing it

      --ttl <DURATION>
          Safety TTL for the solo flag (default 24h); accepts 8h / 30m / 2h30m

      --watch
          Run the solo LOOP in the foreground: the single leave-it-running command that works the
          safe backlog end-to-end on a cadence (garden → assess/queue → implement → integrate →
          repeat), keystone parked. Subsumes `aida queue integrate --watch`. Stops on `aida solo
          --off`, Ctrl-C, or the TTL

      --dry-run
          With `--watch`: run ONE tick that PRINTS the cycle it would execute, then exit — verify
          the loop without running a live drain

      --interval <SECS>
          With `--watch`: seconds between cycles (default 300)
          
          [default: 300]

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida whoami
Print the caller identity AIDA resolved — role, agent-type, agent-name, user-id, headless flag,
ai-tool, and active session/scope — each line annotated with where the value came from (env var vs
fallback vs default). Read-only: it runs the SAME resolvers the gating/queue/ provenance code uses,
so it answers "why did this refuse?" (role resolved to a default, not advisor, tripping the
advisor-gate) and "why is my queue empty?" (your user/role identity differs from what queued the
items). No project store is loaded; no state is written.

Hidden alias for `aida node whoami` (identity introspection lives under the `node` namespace; kept
top-level for muscle memory).

Usage: aida whoami [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida _bg-fetch
(internal) Background fetch worker spawned by `aida statusline`. Fetches `origin/<branch>` for the
orphan store at <store-path>, updates `~/.aida/cache/last-fetch.toml`, and removes the per-project
lockfile. Not intended for direct invocation — statusline forks this as a detached process with
stdio nulled

Usage: aida _bg-fetch [OPTIONS] <STORE_PATH>

Arguments:
  <STORE_PATH>
          Absolute path to the orphan-store worktree (`.aida-store/`)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida upgrade
Upgrade aida to the latest release (or a specified version). Detects how aida was installed (cargo /
pre-built binary) and uses the matching upgrade strategy. From a developer build with no --target,
scans common install locations and offers to upgrade any stale sibling installs

Usage: aida upgrade [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  check  Compare current/sibling versions to latest release
  diff   Print unreleased commit diff from a developer build
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --check
          Compare current/sibling versions to latest release; report only, don't install

      --version <VERSION>
          Install a specific version instead of latest. Format: `v0.4.0`

  -y, --yes
          Skip confirmation prompt

      --target <TARGET>
          Upgrade a specific binary path instead of the currently-running one. Useful from a
          developer shell to upgrade `~/.local/bin/aida` etc

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida rel add
Add a relationship between local requirements

Both positional and flag forms work: aida rel add <from> <to> --type child aida rel add --from
<from> --to <to> --type child

Cross-store references such as `other-project#<SPEC-ID>` are not local graph edges; record them in
comments until AIDA has a resolver.

Usage: aida rel add [OPTIONS] --type <TYPE> [FROM] [TO]

Arguments:
  [FROM]
          Source requirement ID (UUID or SPEC-ID). Positional or via --from

  [TO]
          Target requirement ID (UUID or SPEC-ID). Positional or via --to

Options:
  -t, --type <TYPE>
          Relationship type (parent, child, duplicate, verifies, verified-by, references, or custom)

  -b, --bidirectional
          Create bidirectional relationship (adds inverse relationship automatically)

      --force-parent
          Override the guard that refuses `--type child` when the target (the parent) is in a
          terminal status (Completed/Rejected). Use when intentionally backfilling a forgotten child
          onto a closed epic

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida rel list
List relationships — global by default, or filtered to a specific source/target requirement.

Examples: aida rel list                      # all edges in the graph aida rel list <spec-id>
# outgoing edges from a spec aida rel list --source <spec-id>   # same as positional form aida rel
list --spec <spec-id>     # alias of --source aida rel list --id <spec-id>       # alias of --source
aida rel list --target <spec-id>   # incoming edges (what points AT it) aida rel list --type child
# filter by edge type aida rel list --dangling           # only edges with unresolved targets aida
rel list --type child --dangling   # composable

Usage: aida rel list [OPTIONS] [ID]

Arguments:
  [ID]
          Source requirement ID (UUID or SPEC-ID). Positional alias of --source. When omitted (and
          --target/--source unset), lists every edge in the graph

Options:
      --source <SOURCE>
          Source requirement — same as the positional. Explicit form for scripts that want to be
          unambiguous. `--spec` and `--id` are accepted as aliases so the dominant ID-flag
          convention (used by `db reconcile-status --spec`, etc.) Just Works here too
          
          [aliases: --spec, --id]

      --target <TARGET>
          Target requirement — inverts the query to "what edges point AT this requirement?". Useful
          for "who depends on this epic?"

  -t, --type <TYPE>
          Filter by relationship type (parent, child, duplicate, verifies, verified-by, references,
          or a custom name)

      --dangling
          Only show edges whose target UUID doesn't resolve (deleted-target tombstones from removed
          reqs). Pairs with `aida doctor verify-relationships --repair` to clean them up

      --all
          Include edges between terminal-status (Completed/Rejected) requirements. By default the
          global listing hides them so the view focuses on actionable work, matching `aida list`

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Cap the number of edges shown (0 = no cap). When unset, the unfiltered global listing
          auto-caps to avoid a firehose on large stores and prints a note; a
          source/target/type/dangling filter lifts the auto-cap. Pass an explicit `--limit` to
          override either way

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Usage: aida rel-def [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:

          Requirement ID (UUID or SPEC-ID)

  [CONTENT]
          Comment content (positional argument)

Options:

          Read comment content from a file. Prefer this for text containing backticks or `$()` so

          comment and shown as "via <author>, originally <seat>"

===== aida config
ID configuration commands

Usage: aida config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  show         Show current ID configuration
  format       Set the ID format (single-level or two-level)
  numbering    Set the numbering strategy
  digits       Set the number of digits in IDs
  migrate      Migrate existing SPEC-XXX IDs to new format
  user         Show or update user-level preferences at `~/.aida/preferences.toml`. Currently
               stores: preferred node id (used as default by `aida init`) and a fallback email (used
               when `git config user.email` is unset)
  hints        Show or toggle workflow hints printed inline at state-transition moments (queue
               drained → open PR, session end → start review). No-arg form prints the current
               setting; pass `true` / `false` to persist into `.aida/config.toml [hints]
               workflow_hints`. The env var `AIDA_HINTS=false` overrides the config for the current
               shell without writing to disk
  glyph        Inspect and customize the CLI glyph set — list the symbols, apply a canned theme, or
               override an individual glyph. Writes to `.aida/config.toml` (or `~/.aida/config.toml`
               with `--user`), preserving the rest of the file
  permissions  Inspect the effective launch permission posture for managed agents
  menu         Browse every configurable item in a navigable TUI: per row the knob's name, current
               value, built-in default, where it was set (scope), and a one-line explanation. The
               visual companion to `config show` — same resolved surface, one screen, arrow-key
               navigation. Safe knobs can be edited in place; integrity-floor knobs stay read-only
               or subcommand-only. Needs a TTY; without one it points you at `config show`
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== aida config glyph
Inspect and customize the CLI glyph set — list the symbols, apply a canned theme, or override an
individual glyph. Writes to `.aida/config.toml` (or `~/.aida/config.toml` with `--user`), preserving
the rest of the file

Usage: aida config glyph [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list   List every glyph: name, currently-resolved rendering (honoring the active profile + theme +
         overrides), and the unicode registry default
  theme  Inspect or apply glyph themes. With no NAME (or `theme list`), lists the embedded themes
         each with a one-line preview row. With a NAME, applies that theme — writes `[ui] theme =
         "<name>"` (a clean reference)
  set    Override an individual glyph: writes `[glyphs] <name> = "<value>"`
  unset  Drop a single per-symbol override
  reset  Clear ALL per-symbol overrides (the whole `[glyphs]` table)
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

===== aida trace
Code-to-requirement traceability commands

Usage: aida trace [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  add       Add a trace link from code to a requirement
  list      List trace links for a requirement or file
  remove    Remove a trace link
  scan      Scan source files for AIDA trace annotations
  sweep     Sweep git commits for requirement references
  gate      CI spec-id validity gate: walk a commit range, resolve every `(SPEC-ID)` subject trailer
            against the live requirement graph, and exit non-zero when any commit references a
            SPEC-ID that does not exist or is rejected (a dead/dangling provenance link).
            Mechanical/release commits with no trailer are exempt; plan commits are skipped
  coverage  CI trace-COVERAGE check: walk a diff and report which changed source hunks carry the
            required code-to-spec provenance (an inline trace comment OR a live commit `(SPEC-ID)`
            trailer), per the deterministic coverage definition + exemptions (tests / generated /
            docs / config / vendored / pure-deletion / fmt-only / trivial). Distinct from `gate`,
            which validates the trailer spec-ids; this checks that the changed CODE is traced.
            Report-only by default (CI succeeds); `--block` fails CI on any uncovered coverable
            hunk. `--all` / `--path` switch to whole-tree mode: per Rust file, the functions with no
            trace marker in or directly above them
  check     Trace-ROT detector: scan source for inline code-to-spec trace markers, resolve each
            referenced id against the live requirement graph, and flag dangling traces — markers
            whose target no longer exists (deleted, renumbered) or resolves to a rejected spec.
            Reports total / resolved / dangling + a rot rate. This makes a stale trace go "red" like
            a failing type — the counterpart to `gate` (validates commit trailers) and `coverage`
            (checks the code is traced). Report-only by default (exit 0); `--block` exits non-zero
            when any dangling trace exists, for CI gating
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --range <RANGE>
          Git revision range to scan (e.g. `origin/main..HEAD`). Defaults to
          `<default-branch>..HEAD` (the commits this branch adds), falling back to `HEAD~20..HEAD`
          when no default branch resolves

      --json
          Emit machine-readable JSON instead of human text

      --block
          Fail (exit non-zero) when any coverable changed hunk is uncovered. Default is report-only:
          the report prints but CI succeeds

      --all
          Whole-tree mode over the project: report every Rust function no trace marker claims, per
          file

      --path <PATH>
          Whole-tree mode over one file or directory

      --fail-on <KIND>
          Whole-tree mode only: exit non-zero when the report contains findings of this kind.
          Without it the report always exits 0

          Possible values:
          - uncovered: Any function no trace marker claims

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida trace check
Trace-ROT detector: scan source for inline code-to-spec trace markers, resolve each referenced id
against the live requirement graph, and flag dangling traces — markers whose target no longer exists
(deleted, renumbered) or resolves to a rejected spec. Reports total / resolved / dangling + a rot
rate. This makes a stale trace go "red" like a failing type — the counterpart to `gate` (validates
commit trailers) and `coverage` (checks the code is traced). Report-only by default (exit 0);
`--block` exits non-zero when any dangling trace exists, for CI gating

Usage: aida trace check [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]
          Path to scan (file or directory). Defaults to the project root

Options:
      --json
          Emit machine-readable JSON instead of human text

      --block
          Fail (exit non-zero) when any dangling trace exists. Default is report-only: the report
          prints but the command succeeds

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===== aida review
Drive human review of a held spec, or generate review prompts.

`aida review <SPEC>` is the human-review counterpart to `aida queue work`: it locates the spec's
review surface (an open draft PR, else the branch + commits, else "built locally, never pushed"),
runs a reviewer over the diff against the spec's `## Acceptance` criteria, then presents the verdict
and lets you decide — approve, request changes, open the diff, or defer. It never auto-merges.

The `prompt` / `assemble` subcommands are the review-prompt helpers.

Usage: aida review [OPTIONS] [SPEC] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  watch           Discover new heads and dispatch attested reviews without waiting for CI
  prompt          Generate a markdown review prompt from a set of linked requirements' acceptance
                  criteria. Specs come either from an explicit `--specs` list (CSV) or from the
                  commit-range of a PR/MR (parsed `(REQ-ID)` trailers in commit messages)
  assemble        Assemble active review fragments into a root REVIEW.md file
  record          Record a review verdict for a spec as first-class state
  claim           Mark a pull request as under review, so nothing merges it before your verdict
                  lands
  verdict         Show the recorded review verdict for a spec, if any
  list            List recorded review verdicts
  classes         Count review findings per defect class across every recorded verdict, including
                  archived rounds. Alias of `aida findings classes`
  normalize-shas  One-time repair: expand every abbreviated `reviewed_sha` on disk to its full
                  commit sha where this repo can still resolve it, and mark the rest explicitly
                  unresolvable. Never invents a value and never touches an already-full or sha-less
                  record
  stranded        Report specs stranded by a refusal at the PR's current head: still Done, unheld,
                  unqueued. Read-only by default; `--fix` applies the same protection a fresh
                  refusal gets (merge hold + Needs Attention)
  mode            Turn a temporary review mode on or off, or show its state
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [SPEC]
          Spec to review (a story, task, or bug id). Resolves its review surface, runs a reviewer
          over the diff, and prompts you to decide. Omit when using a `prompt` / `assemble`
          subcommand

Options:
      --no-agent
          Skip the reviewer-agent analysis: just locate + report the review surface and the
          recommended next command. Useful in non-interactive contexts or when you only want the
          diff pointer

      --allow-stale-base
          Skip the stale-base warning. By default, when the spec's PR is behind its base branch, the
          review prints a warning naming the gap and the rebase command (the review still proceeds
          either way). Pass this flag when a deliberately stale review is intended — same opt-out
          the reviewer-role pickup honors

      --target-branch <BRANCH>
          Explicit base branch to target when AC-5 offers to open a change from a branch with no
          open PR/MR. Always wins over any base saved from a previous offer
          (`.aida/mr-recovery/<spec>.json`) — use this to correct a stuck recovery, e.g. when a
          GitLab project's default branch became the feature branch itself because remote `main` was
          never pushed

      --format <FORMAT>
          Pin the output format regardless of whether stdout is a terminal: human = tables, toon =
          compact agent output, json = machine JSON. Default (unset) is human at a TTY, toon when
          piped/captured. Also settable via AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT (the flag wins)

          Possible values:
          - human: Human-readable tables / emoji (the interactive default at a TTY)
          - toon:  Token-efficient TOON — the compact agent default when piped/captured
          - json:  Machine JSON, for commands that support a JSON projection

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
